summary:
Complete extraction of the 125-page paper that introduces prisms and prismatic cohomology. A prism is a pair (A, I) with A a δ-ring — a ring with a p-derivation, equivalently a lift of Frobenius when p-torsionfree — and I a Cartier divisor with A derived (p, I)-complete and p ∈ I + φ(I)A; perfect prisms are the same thing as perfectoid rings, so a prism is a deperfection of a perfectoid ring. For a bounded prism and a smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I the prismatic site (X/A)_∆ has cohomology RΓ_∆(X/A) with a Frobenius, and the paper proves that it specialises to crystalline cohomology when I = (p), to differential forms after reduction modulo I (the Hodge–Tate comparison), to de Rham cohomology after Frobenius-twisted reduction, and to étale cohomology of the generic fibre after inverting I and taking φ-fixed points, with base change along maps of prisms and with Frobenius an isogeny in a precise sense. It then develops the theory for semiperfectoid rings — universal prisms, perfectoidization and its surjectivity, the Nygaard filtration and its identification with the conjugate filtration, and the comparison with π₀TP — and gives three applications: a new proof of the almost purity theorem, in a strengthened form for integral algebras and arbitrary closed subsets; the bound of 1 on the F_p-étale cohomological dimension of Spec(R[1/p]) for R perfectoid; and the resolution of the vanishing conjecture for the syntomic complexes ℤ_p(n), hence that mod-p K-theory is locally concentrated in even degrees. The last three sections construct q-crystalline cohomology, prove that it is computed by the q-de Rham complexes of Scholze and so settles his independence conjecture, identify it with the A_inf-cohomology of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, and prove that prismatic cohomology has no nontrivial endomorphisms, so that all these comparison isomorphisms are compatible. Of the 96 items, 1 is in the pinned libraries, 83 are planned by existing layers, and 12 are missing. The atlas covers this paper unusually well: the PrismaticCohomology roadmap names BS22 section by section in PR.0 (§§2–3), PR.1 (§§4–6), PR.2 (§§7–8), PR.3 (§§12–15), PR.4 (§§9, 11, 14) and PR.6 (§§16–18), and PerfectoidQuotients Q0–Q4 reexport and extend the semiperfectoid half. The extraction is therefore a source proposal for existing layers and not a new roadmap, and the twelve missing items are the two places the coverage stops short: the arc-topology of p-adic formal schemes with its descent results for perfectoidization, and §10's almost purity theorem for integral algebras together with the almost setting attached to an arbitrary finitely generated ideal of a perfectoid ring. Four misprints were found and are recorded under sourceIssues; none affects a proof. This is a paper inventory and routing, not a proof blueprint: the results quoted from Joyal, Borger, André, Gabber–Ramero, Mathew, Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, Bhatt–Mathew and the authors' own earlier work with Morrow are recorded as items or prerequisites and are not decomposed here.

After review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): 148 items (1 library, 121 planned, 26 missing), 6 routes, all accepted as corrected. 31 items were split off from multi-part items, 21 were added for definitions and results the extraction lacked (6 of them missing), and planned citations were corrected on twenty items (among them RT.3 → RT.6 for the trace comparisons, DD.0 → DD.1 and DD.5, and consumer stages removed); items 47 and 53 became missing. The arc-topology goes to the accepted ArcTopologyAndDescent roadmap, the perfectoidization of integral algebras and almost purity along arbitrary ideals (§8.1–8.2, §10) to a new Part II of PerfectoidQuotients, and the K-theoretic corollaries to the accepted RefinedTraceMethods Part II on henselian pairs. The four recorded misprints are confirmed; E5–E30 are new, all misprints except an omitted completeness hypothesis in Lemma 3.7 (E10) and an unproved flatness claim in Construction 6.1 (E13); no stated result of the paper changes.

items.name: δ-ring
items.statement: A δ-ring is a pair (R, δ) with R a commutative ring and δ : R → R a map of sets with δ(0) = δ(1) = 0 satisfying δ(xy) = x^p δ(y) + y^p δ(x) + p δ(x)δ(y) and δ(x+y) = δ(x) + δ(y) + (x^p + y^p − (x+y)^p)/p. Equivalently (Remark 2.4), a δ-structure on R is a ring map w : R → W₂(R) splitting the projection ε : W₂(R) → R, where W₂(R) = R × R with the p-typical length-two Witt vector operations. All rings in the paper are ℤ_(p)-algebras (§2, p. 13).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 2.1 and Remark 2.4, p. 13
items.note: The basic object of the paper; δ-structures are Joyal's p-typical λ-structures and Buium's p-derivations. Planned by PR.0, whose first sentence is 'Construct p-derivations/delta-rings, free delta-algebras and Frobenius lifts'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the paper's standing convention that all rings are ℤ_(p)-algebras was added.

items.name: δ-structures and Frobenius lifts
items.statement: For a δ-ring (R, δ) the map φ(x) := x^p + p δ(x) is a ring homomorphism lifting the Frobenius of R/p. If R is p-torsionfree, then conversely every lift φ : R → R of the Frobenius on R/p comes from a unique δ-structure, given by δ(x) = (φ(x) − x^p)/p. A δ-ring over ℚ is just a ℚ-algebra with an endomorphism. Moreover (Remark 2.5), for a ℤ_(p)-algebra R a δ-structure is the same as a map φ : R → R together with a path in End_{SCR_{F_p}}(R ⊗^L_ℤ F_p) between φ and the Frobenius, i.e. a lift of Frobenius in the derived sense.
items.note: PR.0 is explicit that this equivalence holds 'only in p-torsionfree rings; a congruence modulo p alone does not determine a delta-structure with p-torsion', so both the statement and its failure are planned there. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Remark 2.5 (the derived-Frobenius-lift description) is not named by PR.0, whose text plans only the p-torsionfree equivalence; it is recorded but not needed later.

items.name: Limits and colimits of δ-rings; Witt vectors as the right adjoint
items.statement: The category of δ-rings has all limits and colimits, computed on underlying rings, so the forgetful functor to rings has both adjoints. The right adjoint is the p-typical Witt vector functor W(−) (Joyal), giving a natural δ-map w_R : R → W(R) whose first two Witt coordinates are x ↦ (x, δ(x)).
items.note: PR.0 plans free δ-algebras, and Q0 asks to 'use existing Witt-vector constructions and compare every Frobenius lift with them'. Witt vectors themselves are in the pinned libraries. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Lemma 2.11 (free δ-rings) was split off as item 3b. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the Q0 citation now names the substage that says 'Use existing Witt-vector constructions and compare every Frobenius lift with them'.

items.name: Free δ-rings
items.statement: ℤ_(p){x} is a polynomial ring on {x, δ(x), δ²(x), …} with faithfully flat Frobenius, and ℚ{x} = ℤ_(p){x}[1/p] is a polynomial ring on {x, φ(x), φ²(x), …}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 3). PR.0 plans free δ-algebras.

items.name: Quotients of δ-rings
items.statement: Let A be a δ-ring. An ideal I ⊂ A is stable under δ if and only if A/I carries a (then unique) compatible δ-structure; the universal δ-A-algebra killing I is A/J with J the δ-stabilization of I (Lemma 2.9, Example 2.10).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 2.9 and Example 2.10, p. 15
items.note: The basic stability toolkit. Lemma 2.18 is used again and again — it is what makes the functor from the prismatic site to the étale site cocontinuous (Construction 4.4). Planned by PR.0. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into four: 4 (Lemma 2.9), 4b (Lemma 2.15 with Remark 2.16), 4c (Lemma 2.17) and 4d (Lemma 2.18). the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Localizations of δ-rings
items.statement: If S ⊂ A is multiplicative with φ(S) ⊂ S, then S^{-1}A has a unique compatible δ-structure and is initial among δ-A-algebras inverting S (Lemma 2.15). If p ∈ rad(A), then φ carries units to units, so (S^{-1}A)_(p) carries a unique compatible δ-structure and is initial among δ-A-algebras B with p ∈ rad(B) in which S becomes invertible (Remark 2.16).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 2.15 and Remark 2.16, pp. 16–17
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 4). Remark 2.16 is used in the proof of Lemma 3.1 ((2) ⇒ (3)). the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Completions of δ-rings
items.statement: If I ⊂ A is finitely generated and contains p, then δ is I-adically continuous and the classical I-adic completion carries a unique compatible δ-structure.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 4). the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Completely étale algebras over δ-rings
items.statement: Let I ⊂ A be finitely generated with p ∈ I. If B is derived I-complete and I-completely étale over A, then B carries a unique δ-structure compatible with that of A. In particular the δ-structure passes uniquely to the derived I-completion for any such I.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 4). The hypothesis 'I finitely generated and containing p' was missing in the extraction. The proof uses Elkik's algebraization (item 86b) to reduce to the derived I-completion of an étale A-algebra. Lemma 2.18 makes the functor of Construction 4.4 cocontinuous. the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: The Frobenius is fpqc-locally surjective, and Joyal's δ_n operations
items.statement: For a δ-ring A and x ∈ A there is a faithfully flat map A → B of δ-rings with x = φ(y) for some y ∈ B (Corollary 2.12). The map w : R → W(R) gives functorial operations δ_n : R → R with w(x) = (δ₀(x), δ₁(x), …), characterised by φⁿ(x) = δ₀(x)^{pⁿ} + p δ₁(x)^{p^{n−1}} + … + pⁿ δ_n(x); δ_n is a monic degree-n polynomial in δ, so ℤ_(p){x} is the polynomial ring on {δ_n(x)}_{n≥0}.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Corollary 2.12 and Remarks 2.13, 2.14, p. 16
items.note: Corollary 2.12 is the source of the flat covers that make the prismatic site work; the δ_n-description of the free δ-ring is used in §18. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Distinguished elements
items.statement: An element d of a δ-ring A is distinguished if δ(d) is a unit. Any morphism of δ-rings preserves distinguished elements. The initial δ-ring with a distinguished element is the localization ℤ_(p){d, δ(d)^{-1}} := S^{-1}ℤ_(p){d} with S = {δ(d), φ(δ(d)), …}, in which the universal distinguished element is a nonzerodivisor modulo p.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 2.19 and Example 2.21, p. 18
items.note: PR.0: 'Construct distinguished elements, maps of prisms, orientations, boundedness'. Distinguishedness is what replaces the prime p in the definition of a prism.

items.name: The four basic distinguished elements
items.statement: (1) Crystalline: A = ℤ_p, d = p, δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} a unit. (2) q-de Rham: A = ℤ_p⟦q−1⟧ with φ(q) = q^p and d = [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1). (3) A_inf: for a perfectoid field C/ℚ_p, A = A_inf(O_C) and d = ξ a generator of ker(θ). (4) Breuil–Kisin: for K/ℚ_p complete discretely valued with perfect residue field k and uniformizer π, A = W(k)⟦u⟧ with φ extending the Frobenius of W(k) and φ(u) = u^p, and d any generator of the kernel of A → O_K, u ↦ π [Example 2.20(4) omits 'complete' and 'perfect residue field', which Example 1.3(3) has; sourceIssues E8].
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Example 2.20, p. 18; Example 1.3, pp. 2–3
items.note: These four examples organise the whole paper, and PR.0 names exactly these as its acceptance examples: '(W(k),(p)), (A_inf,ker theta), the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]],(E(u))), and (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)) with phi(q)=q^p'. PR.0 also warns that 'the q-prism ideal is [p]_q, not q−1'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the Breuil–Kisin example now carries the hypotheses of Example 1.3(3) (E8).

items.name: Unit multiples of distinguished elements
items.statement: Let A be a δ-ring. If d ∈ A is distinguished, u ∈ A^× and d, p ∈ rad(A), then ud is distinguished.
items.note: Lemma 2.25 is the reason the condition 'p ∈ I + φ(I)A' in the definition of a prism is intrinsic to the ideal, and Lemma 2.24 is used in the proof of Theorem 3.10. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 8 (Lemma 2.23), 8b (Lemma 2.24) and 8c (Lemma 2.25).

items.name: Factors of distinguished elements
items.statement: Let A be a δ-ring, d ∈ A distinguished and d = fh with f, p ∈ rad(A). Then f is distinguished and h is a unit.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 8). Used in the proof of Theorem 3.10.

items.name: Distinguishedness depends only on the ideal
items.statement: Let A be a δ-ring and d ∈ A with d, p ∈ rad(A). Then d is distinguished if and only if p ∈ (d, φ(d)); in particular distinguishedness depends only on the ideal (d).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 8). The reason the condition p ∈ I + φ(I)A in the definition of a prism is intrinsic to the ideal.

items.name: Perfect δ-rings and perfection
items.statement: A δ-ring A is perfect if φ is an isomorphism. The inclusion of perfect δ-rings into δ-rings has both adjoints, A ↦ A_perf = colim_φ A and A ↦ A^perf = lim_φ A.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 2.26 and Remark 2.27, p. 20
items.note: PR.0 plans 'completed perfection' and the perfect case; the Witt-vector equivalence is the input to Theorem 3.10. Remark 2.29 shows the two hypotheses of Lemma 2.28 are incomparable: ℤ_p[x]/(x^p − 1) is reduced with non-injective φ, and ℤ_p[x]/(x²) is non-reduced with injective φ. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 9 (Definition 2.26, Remark 2.27), 9b (Lemma 2.28 with Remark 2.29) and 9c (Corollary 2.31).

items.name: Perfect δ-rings are p-torsionfree
items.statement: Let A be a δ-ring. If px = 0 then φ(x) = 0; hence A is p-torsionfree if φ is injective or if A is reduced (Lemma 2.28). The two hypotheses are incomparable: ℤ_p[x]/(x^p − 1) is reduced with non-injective φ, and ℤ_p[x]/(x²) is non-reduced with injective φ (Remark 2.29).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 2.28 and Remark 2.29, p. 20
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 9).

items.name: The Witt vector equivalence for perfect δ-rings
items.statement: The categories of perfect p-complete δ-rings, of p-adically complete p-torsionfree rings A with A/p perfect, and of perfect F_p-algebras are equivalent, via the forgetful functor, A ↦ A/p and R ↦ W(R); in particular every ring homomorphism between perfect p-complete δ-rings is a δ-map, and W(R) carries a unique δ-structure for R a perfect F_p-algebra.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 9). The input to Theorem 3.10. Mathlib has W(R), its completeness and the Teichmüller series (item 88), but not the δ-structure or the universal property.

items.name: Elements with all p-power roots have rank one
items.statement: For a δ-ring A and x ∈ A one has δ(x^{pⁿ}) ∈ pⁿA for all n; hence if A is p-adically separated and y admits pⁿ-th roots for all n, then δ(y) = 0, i.e. y has rank one.
items.note: Lemma 2.34 is what makes perfect prisms bounded, and Lemma 2.33 is the concrete description used in the proof of Theorem 3.10. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 10 (Lemma 2.32), 10b (Lemma 2.33) and 10c (Lemma 2.34). the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Distinguished elements of perfect δ-rings
items.statement: Let A = W(R) be a perfect p-complete δ-ring and d = Σ_i [a_i]p^i ∈ A. Then d is distinguished if and only if a₁ is a unit of R.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 10). Used in the proof of Theorem 3.10. the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Distinguished elements are nonzerodivisors
items.statement: If A is a p-torsionfree, p-adically separated δ-ring with A/p reduced and d ∈ A is distinguished, then d is a nonzerodivisor and R = A/d satisfies R[p] = R[p^∞].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 10). What makes perfect prisms bounded. the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Divided powers in δ-rings: the model case
items.statement: Let A be a p-torsionfree δ-ring and z ∈ A with γ_p(z) = z^p/p! ∈ A; then γ_n(z) ∈ A for all n (Lemma 2.35). The ring C := ℤ_(p){x, φ(x)/p}, defined as the pushout of ℤ_(p){y} → ℤ_(p){z}, y ↦ pz, along y ↦ φ(x), identifies with the pd-envelope D_{(x)}(ℤ_(p){x}) (Lemma 2.36), and the simplicial commutative ring obtained by freely adjoining φ(x)/p to ℤ_(p){x} is discrete, so the pushout is also one of simplicial commutative rings (Remark 2.37, corrected as in sourceIssues E3).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemmas 2.35, 2.36 and Remark 2.37, pp. 22–24
items.note: The bridge to crystalline cohomology. Remark 2.40 adds that D_I(A) is the φ-pullback of A{f₁/p,…,f_r/p}, which depends only on the ideal and gives PD-envelopes a canonical φ-descent; Warning 2.41 shows that without the Frobenius twist the subring of A[1/p] does depend on the δ-structure. PR.0 says 'Compare with the PD envelopes already built in CR.0'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 11 (Lemmas 2.35–2.36, Remark 2.37), 11b (Lemma 2.38) and 11c (Corollary 2.39, Remark 2.40); Lemma 2.35, which Lemma 2.36 needs, was added.

items.name: Divided power envelopes of Koszul-regular sequences
items.statement: Let B be p-torsionfree and f₁, …, f_r ∈ B Koszul-regular on B/p. Then the pushout of B along ℤ_(p)[x₁,…,x_r] → D_{(x)}(ℤ_(p)[x₁,…,x_r]), x_i ↦ f_i, in simplicial commutative rings is discrete, p-torsionfree and equal to D_{(f₁,…,f_r)}(B); its formation commutes with base change along maps B → B′ of p-torsionfree rings such that f₁, …, f_r is Koszul-regular on B′/p.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 11). The base-change clause had lost the hypothesis on B′.

items.name: PD-envelopes of regular sequences in δ-rings
items.statement: If A is a p-torsionfree δ-ring and f₁, …, f_r is regular in A/p, then the simplicial commutative δ-ring A{φ(f₁)/p, …, φ(f_r)/p} is discrete, p-torsionfree and equals the PD-envelope D_I(A) of I = (f₁,…,f_r); so D_I(A) is a δ-ring, finitely presented as such (Corollary 2.39). D_I(A) is the φ-pullback of A{f₁/p,…,f_r/p}, which gives PD-envelopes a canonical φ-descent (Remark 2.40); without the Frobenius twist the subring of A[1/p] depends on the δ-structure (Warning 2.41).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Corollary 2.39, Remark 2.40 and Warning 2.41, pp. 25–26
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 11). The bridge to crystalline cohomology; PR.0: 'Compare with the PD envelopes already built in CR.0'. It uses simplicial commutative δ-rings (item 97).

items.name: Completely regular sequences relative to a base
items.statement: For a simplicial commutative ring A with a finitely generated ideal I = (f₁, …, f_n) ⊂ π₀(A) and a derived I-complete simplicial commutative A-algebra B, a sequence x₁, …, x_r ∈ π₀(B) is I-completely regular relative to A if Kos(A; f₁,…,f_n) → Kos(B; f₁,…,f_n, x₁,…,x_r) is a flat map of simplicial commutative rings.
items.note: The relative flatness statements that make the prismatic envelopes of Proposition 3.13 flat. PR.0 asks for 'complete flatness and regularity under the source hypotheses' and explicitly warns against 'treating every ideal as Cartier'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 12 (Definition 2.42), 12b (Lemma 2.43) and 12c (Corollary 2.44); the generators and the completeness of B were made explicit. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): DD.0 does not plan relative complete regularity; DD.1 does ('Prove the bounded-torsion criteria used for bounded prisms, complete flatness and complete faithful-flat descent').

items.name: Complete flatness of divided-power adjunctions
items.statement: If x₁^p, …, x_r^p is p-completely regular relative to A, then the p-complete pushout of B along the PD-envelope of (y₁,…,y_r) in ℤ_p[y₁,…,y_r]^∧ (y_i ↦ x_i) is p-completely flat over A.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 12).

items.name: Complete flatness of free adjunction of x_i/p
items.statement: If A → B are p-complete simplicial commutative δ-rings and x₁, …, x_r ∈ π₀(B) is p-completely regular relative to A, then B{x₁/p, …, x_r/p}^∧ is p-completely flat over A.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 12). The relative flatness behind the prismatic envelopes of Proposition 3.13.

items.name: Equivalent formulations of the prism condition
items.statement: Let A be a δ-ring and I ⊂ A a locally principal ideal with p, I ⊂ rad(A). The following are equivalent: p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A; p ∈ I + φ(I)A; there is a faithfully flat ind-(Zariski localization) A → A' of δ-rings with IA' = (d) for a distinguished d with d, p ∈ rad(A').
items.note: This is what lets the definition of a prism be checked after a flat cover and reduced to the oriented case. Planned by PR.0.

items.name: Prisms: bounded, perfect, orientable, crystalline
items.statement: A prism is a pair (A, I) with A a δ-ring and I ⊂ A defining a Cartier divisor on Spec(A), such that A is derived (p, I)-complete and p ∈ I + φ(I)A. A prism is perfect if φ is an isomorphism, bounded if A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, orientable if I is principal (a generator being an orientation), and crystalline if I = (p). A map (A, I) → (B, J) of prisms is (faithfully) flat if A → B is (p, I)-completely (faithfully) flat. Crystalline prisms are exactly the pairs (A, (p)) with A p-torsionfree and p-complete. A map (A, I) → (B, J) of prisms is a map A → B of δ-rings carrying I into J (Definition 1.1); crystalline prisms are bounded and orientable (Definition 3.2).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definitions 1.1, 1.4 and 3.2, Example 3.3, pp. 2–3 and 28–29
items.note: The central definition of the paper. Boundedness is a technical restriction adopted to control completions in non-noetherian situations and to avoid derived prisms. PR.0 plans exactly these notions and asks for 'a delta-ring that is not a prism' as an acceptance test — the paper's example is W(F_p[x]/(x²)), in which every nonzerodivisor is a unit.

items.name: The universal oriented prism
items.statement: Let A₀ = ℤ_(p){d, δ(d)^{-1}} and let A be its (p, d)-completion, I = (d). Then (A, I) is a bounded prism, d is a distinguished generator, and (A, I) is the universal oriented prism (though not the universal orientable one). In this prism the sequence p, d is regular and φ : A/p → A/p is d-completely flat.
items.note: The base over which the Hodge–Tate comparison is first proved in §6; the d-complete flatness of φ on A/p is what makes Construction 6.1 work. Planned by PR.0. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Example 3.4 proves only that φ on A/p is d-completely flat, which is what Construction 6.1 uses (sourceIssues E13).

items.name: Rigidity of maps of prisms
items.statement: If (A, I) → (B, J) is a map of prisms, then I ⊗_A B → J is an isomorphism; in particular J = IB. Conversely, if A → B is a map of δ-rings with B derived (p, I)-complete, then (B, IB) is a prism exactly when B[I] = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 3.5 and Proposition 1.5, pp. 3 and 29
items.note: Rigidity is what makes the prismatic site over a fixed base well behaved: the ideal does not vary, so O_∆ ⊗_A A/I = Ō_∆. PR.0 names 'the rigidity I B=J for a prism map'.

items.name: The Frobenius twist of a prism ideal is principal
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism. Then φ(I)A is principal with distinguished generators, and φ^*(I) and I^p are trivial invertible A-modules.
items.note: Local orientability, Lemma 3.7 (4), is the standard reduction step: every statement about bounded prisms may be checked after a faithfully flat base change to an oriented one. Planned by PR.0. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 17 (Lemma 3.6), 17b (Lemma 3.7 with the descent paragraph after it) and 17c (Lemma 3.8).

items.name: Structure of bounded prisms
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (1) A is classically (p, I)-complete. (2) Every derived (p, I)-complete, (p, I)-completely flat M ∈ D(A) is discrete and classically (p, I)-complete, with M[Iⁿ] = 0 and M/IⁿM of bounded p^∞-torsion for all n. (3) Flat maps of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) are the same as derived (p, I)-complete, (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebras B, via B ↦ (B, IB). (4) (A, I) admits a (p, I)-completely faithfully flat map to an oriented bounded prism, the completion of an ind-Zariski localization. Derived (p, I)-complete, (p, I)-completely flat complexes form a sheaf on bounded prisms for the flat topology, and on bounded prisms they are modules.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 3.7 and the paragraph after it, pp. 29–30
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 17). The paper omits 'derived (p, I)-complete' in (2) and (3); without it Q_p over (ℤ_p, (p)) is a counterexample (sourceIssues E10). The descent paragraph is used in the proof of Proposition 3.13.

items.name: Perfect prisms are bounded
items.statement: A perfect prism has principal I with distinguished generators, and is bounded.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 17).

items.name: Perfection of a prism
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism and A_perf = colim_φ A. Then IA_perf = (d) for a distinguished d, d and p are nonzerodivisors in A_perf, and A_perf/d[p^∞] = A_perf/d[p]. Consequently the derived (p, I)-completion A_∞ agrees with the classical one, and (A, I)_perf := (A_∞, IA_∞) is the universal perfect prism under (A, I).
items.note: PR.0 names 'the perfection theorem BS22 3.9' among the results Q0 imports from it.

items.name: Perfectoid rings are the same as perfect prisms
items.statement: The category of perfectoid rings R and the category of perfect prisms (A, I) are equivalent, via R ↦ (A_inf(R), ker θ) and (A, I) ↦ A/I. Perfectoid rings are meant in the sense of [BMS1, §3].
items.note: The theorem that justifies calling a prism a deperfection of a perfectoid ring. PR.0 is emphatic that this 'is a new theorem, not a definition declaring the categories equivalent', and asks that it be proved 'using the existing integral perfectoid/tilt/A_inf construction'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Q0 imports this equivalence ('Import its proved correspondence between perfect prisms and integral perfectoid rings'); it does not plan it, so only PR.0 is cited.

items.name: Perfectoid covers of complete regular local rings
items.statement: Let R be a complete noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic with residue field k of characteristic p. Writing R = A/(f) with A = W⟦x₁,…,x_d⟧ for a Cohen ring W, one can choose a δ-structure on A making f distinguished, so that (A, (f)) is a prism; the Frobenius on A is p-completely faithfully flat, so the perfection (A_∞, (f)) gives a perfectoid ring R_∞ = A_∞/(f) with R → R_∞ faithfully flat.
items.note: A prismatic account of the perfectoid covers of André and Bhatt. The case distinction turns on whether the coefficient of p in f modulo the square of the maximal ideal vanishes. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: The site of all bounded prisms
items.statement: The opposite of the category of bounded prisms, with covers the faithfully flat maps of prisms, is a site; the functors (A, I) ↦ A and (A, I) ↦ A/I are sheaves with vanishing higher cohomology on every object.
items.note: This is what makes the prismatic site of Definition 4.1 a site and O_∆, Ō_∆ sheaves. Planned by PR.1, which asks for 'the sheaf property' of the relative site.

items.name: Existence of prismatic envelopes for regular ideals
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, B a derived (p, I)-complete, (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebra and J ⊂ B an ideal containing IB such that Zariski-locally on Spf(B) one can write J = (I, x₁,…,x_r) with x₁,…,x_r being (p, I)-completely regular relative to A. Then there is a universal map (B, J) → (C, IC) of δ-pairs to a prism over (A, I), written C = B{J/I}^∧; it is (p, I)-completely flat over (A, I), its formation commutes with base change along maps of bounded prisms, and it is compatible with flat localization on B: if B → B′ is a (p, I)-completely flat map of δ-A-algebras, then B{J/I}^∧ ⊗̂^L_B B′ ≅ B′{JB′/I}^∧.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proposition 3.13 and Example 3.14, pp. 33–35
items.note: The technical engine of §4: prismatic envelopes give the weakly initial objects that compute prismatic cohomology by Čech–Alexander complexes. PR.0: 'Construct prismatic envelopes by delta adjunction and derived completion, prove their universal properties, complete flatness and regularity under the source hypotheses.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the completeness of B and the exact form of the localization clause were made explicit.

items.name: The prismatic site and its two structure sheaves
items.statement: Fix a bounded prism (A, I) and a p-adic formal scheme X over A/I. The prismatic site (X/A)_∆ is the opposite of the category of maps (A, I) → (B, IB) of bounded prisms together with a map Spf(B/IB) → X over A/I, with covers the faithfully flat maps of prisms. The structure sheaf O_∆ sends such an object to B, and the reduced structure sheaf Ō_∆ sends it to B/IB; by rigidity O_∆ ⊗_A A/I ≅ Ō_∆. The main theorems require X to be smooth over A/I. O_∆ is a sheaf of I-torsionfree δ-A-algebras, and RΓ_∆(X/A) := RΓ((X/A)_∆, O_∆) is a commutative algebra in D(A) with the φ_A-linear endomorphism φ induced by the Frobenius lift of O_∆.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definitions 1.6 and 4.1 and the preamble of Theorem 1.8, pp. 3–4 and 36
items.note: PR.1: 'For bounded (A,I) and p-completely smooth R over A/I, construct the relative prismatic site with its complete faithfully-flat covers, structure sheaf, reduced structure sheaf, and map to the scheme's étale site.' Remark 4.5 notes that the Zariski, Nisnevich and étale topologies compute the same cohomology, and explains that the flat topology is chosen to leave room for quasisyntomic descent from perfectoid situations.

items.name: The prismatic topos as a slice topos, and the map to the étale site
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The prismatic topos Shv((X/A)_∆) is the slice of Shv((*/A)_∆) over the sheaf h_X(B, IB) = Hom_{A/I}(Spf(B/IB), X), which makes its functoriality in X transparent (Remark 4.3). There is a cocontinuous functor µ : (X/A)_∆ → fSch_{/X} sending (B, IB) to Spf(B/IB) → X — cocontinuity is Lemma 2.18 — hence morphisms of topoi µ_X : Shv((X/A)_∆) → Shv(fSch_{/X}) and ν_X : Shv((X/A)_∆) → Shv(X_ét), with (ν_*F)(U → X) = H⁰((U/A)_∆, F).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Remark 4.3 and Construction 4.4, p. 37
items.note: The functor ν is what localises prismatic cohomology on X_ét and is needed even to state the non-affine Hodge–Tate comparison. PR.1 plans the 'map to the scheme's étale site'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the standing hypotheses of §4 were added to the statement.

items.name: Variants: the perfect and the absolute prismatic site
items.statement: The perfect prismatic site (Y/A)_∆^perf is the full subcategory of objects whose prism is perfect; equivalently, the category of perfectoid rings over A/I with a map Spf(R) → Y, a description not mentioning prisms (Remark 4.6). The absolute prismatic site (X)_∆ has as objects bounded prisms (B, J) with a map Spf(B/J) → X, with no base prism (Remark 4.7).
items.note: The perfect site is analysed in §8 and the absolute site is the subject of Bhatt–Lurie. PR.2 plans perfect-prismatic cohomology; PR.5 plans the absolute site and its comparison with the relative ones. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Lemma 4.8 was split off as item 25b.

items.name: Perfect prisms are initial in the absolute prismatic site
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I. For any prism (B, J), every ring map A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J); hence A is initial in (R)_∆ and (R)_∆ = (R/A)_∆. The dual statement fails.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 25). Used throughout §§7–9. It follows from Theorem 3.10 and Corollary 2.31 (items 19, 9c), which PR.0 plans.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate comparison map and the Bockstein differential
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Set ∆_{X/A} := Rν_*O_∆ ∈ D(X_ét, A) and ∆̄_{X/A} := Rν_*Ō_∆ ∈ D(X_ét, O_X), so that ∆̄_{X/A} ≅ ∆_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. Writing M{i} := M ⊗_{A/I} I^i/I^{i+1}, the triangle ∆̄{i+1} → ∆_{X/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → ∆̄{i} gives a Bockstein differential β_I : H^i(∆̄_{X/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(∆̄_{X/A}){i+1}, making H^*(∆̄_{X/A}){*} a differential graded A/I-algebra. The universal properties of Kähler differentials and of the de Rham complex then produce a map of commutative differential graded algebras η_X^* : Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} → H^*(∆̄_{X/A}){*}, once one knows that β_I(f) squares to zero (Lemma 4.10). For X = Spf(R) one writes ∆_{R/A} := RΓ(Spf R, ∆_{Spf R/A}) and ∆̄_{R/A} := ∆_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I (Notation 4.16, which prints Spec for Spf and 'A = R/I' for 'R = A/I'; sourceIssues E12).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Construction 4.9 and Lemma 4.10, p. 39
items.note: Lemma 4.10 is non-obvious only when p = 2 and is deduced later from Proposition 6.2. PR.1 asks to 'Construct its multiplicative map and the Bockstein differential'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the standing hypotheses of §4 were added to the statement.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate comparison
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The map η_X^* : Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} → H^*(∆̄_{X/A}){*} is an isomorphism of differential graded A/I-algebras; in particular ∆̄_{X/A} is a perfect complex with H^i(∆̄_{X/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}{−i}. In the affine case X = Spf(R) this reads Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(RΓ_∆(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorems 1.8 (2), 4.11 and 6.3, pp. 4, 40 and 52
items.note: The fundamental structural result: prismatic cohomology has a Hodge–Tate filtration with differential forms as graded pieces, so it is a perfect complex for X proper. PR.1: 'Prove the Hodge–Tate comparison on affines: H^i(Δ tensor^L_A A/I) is Ω^i with twist (I/I²)^(-i).' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the standing hypotheses of §4 were added to the statement.

items.name: Base change for prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. For a map (A, I) → (B, IB) of bounded prisms with g : X_B = X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Spf(B/IB) → X, the derived (p, I)-completion of g^*∆_{X/A} is ∆_{X_B/B}; equivalently RΓ_∆(X/A) ⊗̂^L_A B ≅ RΓ_∆(Y/B).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Corollary 4.12 and Theorem 1.8 (5), pp. 4 and 40
items.note: Deduced from the Hodge–Tate comparison. PR.1: 'Prove completed base change along bounded prism maps'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the standing hypotheses of §4 were added to the statement.

items.name: The cotangent complex as a truncation of Hodge–Tate cohomology
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. There is a natural isomorphism L_{X/A} ≅ τ^{≤1}∆̄_{X/A}{1}[1] of p-complete cotangent complexes. Consequently the map O_X → τ^{≤1}∆̄_{X/A} splits as a map of O_X-modules if and only if X lifts to A/I².
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proposition 4.15 and Remark 4.14, pp. 40–41
items.note: Remark 4.13 adds the Higgs specialization: if A is p-torsionfree and X lifts to a (p, I)-completely flat formal scheme 𝔛 over A with a compatible Frobenius lift, one obtains a φ-equivariant map ∆_{X/A} → O_𝔛, whose reduction mod I splits O_X → ∆̄_{X/A} and depends on 𝔛, and hence a dictionary between prismatic crystals and topologically nilpotent Higgs fields. Remark 15.6 upgrades Proposition 4.15 to L_{X/A} ≅ gr¹_N ∆_{X/A}^{(1)}. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the standing hypotheses of §4 were added to the statement. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Proposition 4.15 has only a proof sketch (p. 41), whose H⁰/H¹ compatibility is left to the reader; a full proof is Anschütz–Le Bras, Prop. 3.2.1. PR.3 was dropped from the citation: its text does not plan this statement, and the Remark 15.6 upgrade is part of the §15 material PR.3 lists. the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§4–6 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Weakly initial objects and Čech–Alexander complexes
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. Choose a surjection B₀ → R with B₀ the derived (p, I)-completion of a polynomial A-algebra. Let B be the derived (equivalently classical) (p, I)-completion of the free δ-A-algebra on B₀, J₀ = ker(B₀ → R) and R′ = (B/J₀B)^∧_p, which is p-completely ind-smooth over A/I, and let C be the prismatic envelope (Proposition 3.13) of (B, ker(B → R′)). Then (C → C/IC ← R) is weakly initial in (R/A)_∆, and the construction is functorial in B₀ and takes tensor products to coproducts (Construction 4.17). Applied to the completed Čech nerve B₀^• of A → B₀ it gives the Čech nerve C^• of C⁰, and C^• (resp. C^•/IC^•) computes ∆_{R/A} (resp. ∆̄_{R/A}) (Construction 4.18). With B₀ the completed polynomial algebra on the set R this is strictly functorial but not base-change compatible; for R = A/I⟨X⟩ and B₀ = A[X]^∧, C^• commutes with base change in (A, I) (Remark 4.19).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Constructions 4.17 and 4.18 and Remark 4.19, pp. 41–43
items.note: The acknowledgements record that Teruhisa Koshikawa pointed out an error, and a fix, in the construction of these Čech–Alexander complexes, now incorporated in Construction 4.18. PR.1: 'Construct Cech–Alexander envelope models, hyperdescent and the Frobenius on derived global sections; prove coordinate independence.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): B₀ must be the completion of a polynomial A-algebra, not merely (p, I)-completely smooth: weak initiality uses a lift B₀ → D to every test object.

items.name: Base change for affine prismatic cohomology along maps of finite Tor amplitude
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. If (A, I) → (A′, I′) is a map of bounded prisms with finite (p, I)-complete Tor amplitude, then the completed base change of ∆_{R/A} is ∆_{R′/A′}, where R′ is the p-completed base change of R.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 31 (Lemma 4.20), 31b (Lemma 4.21, corrected) and 31c (Lemma 4.22).

items.name: Étale localization of Hodge–Tate cohomology
items.statement: If R → S is a p-completely étale map of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras, then the natural map ∆̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R S → ∆̄_{S/A} is an isomorphism.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 31). The extraction stated it for ∆_{R/A}, which is not an R-module. It is the étale-localization step reducing Theorem 6.3 to p-completed polynomial algebras.

items.name: Completed base change commutes with totalizations
items.statement: Completed base change along a map of finite J-complete Tor amplitude commutes with totalizations of cosimplicial objects in D^{≥0}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 31). The device for passing base change through Čech–Alexander totalizations.

items.name: The crystalline comparison in characteristic p
items.statement: Let (A, (p)) be a crystalline prism, I ⊂ A a pd-ideal containing p, so that Frobenius factors as ψ : A/I → A/p; let R be a smooth A/I-algebra and R^{(1)} = R ⊗_{A/I, ψ} A/p. Then there is a canonical isomorphism ∆_{R^{(1)}/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A) of E_∞-A-algebras, compatible with Frobenius. Here RΓ_crys(R/A) is crystalline cohomology relative to the pd-thickening Spec(A/I) ⊂ Spf(A). In particular (Remark 5.3 with Corollary 4.12, and Theorem 1.8 (1)), for I = (p) and R̃ smooth over A/p, φ_A^*∆_{R̃/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R̃/A).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 5.2 and Theorem 1.8 (1), pp. 4 and 45
items.note: Note the Frobenius twist: prismatic cohomology is a canonical Frobenius descent of crystalline cohomology, which for A a smooth lift with a Frobenius lift is genuinely extra information and constrains the torsion in crystalline cohomology. PR.1: 'Prove the crystalline comparison for I=(p) using CR.2's PD Poincare lemma, with its phi_A-twisted scalar extension.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): 'Equivalently' overstated the relation to Theorem 1.8(1), and the crystalline base was not named. The Frobenius compatibility is only sketched in the paper ('we do not know a reference, so we sketch a proof', p. 46), and the independence of the lift R̃ is left to the reader (p. 47).

items.name: A cosimplicial descent lemma along the relative Frobenius
items.statement: Let k be a ring of characteristic p, B a polynomial k-algebra, B^• the Čech nerve of k → B and B^{•,(1)} its Frobenius twist. For any cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module N the map N → N ⊗_{B^{•,(1)}} B^• is a quasi-isomorphism on associated unnormalized chain complexes of k-modules.
items.note: The technical heart of the characteristic-p comparison; the proof uses that degeneracy maps may be ignored in the derived category, and the authors note that a better proof would be desirable. A similar statement is in work of Nizioł. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§4–6 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate comparison in characteristic p
items.statement: Let (A, (p)) be a crystalline prism. For every smooth A/p-algebra S the Hodge–Tate comparison map is an isomorphism, H^i(∆̄_{S/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/p)}{−i}; in particular S ↦ ∆_{S/A} commutes with arbitrary p-complete base change of (A, (p)).
items.note: The characteristic-p case of Theorem 4.11, deduced from the crystalline comparison, and the base case of the mixed-characteristic argument of §6. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the base prism was made explicit. The proof uses the Cartier isomorphism for polynomial F_p-algebras (item 101).

items.name: Mapping the universal oriented prism to a crystalline one
items.statement: Let (A, (d)) be an oriented prism with A/(d) p-torsionfree and the Frobenius of A/p flat (d-complete flatness suffices; sourceIssues E13), for example the universal oriented prism of Example 3.4. Let B := A{φ(d)/p}^∧; it is (p, d)-complete, discrete, p-torsionfree and equal to the p-completed pd-envelope of (d) ⊂ A (Corollary 2.39). Let α = (A → B)∘φ_A. Then α(d) ∈ pB, so α : (A, (d)) → (B, (p)) is a map of prisms; modulo p it factors as A/p → A/(p, d) →^φ A/(p, d^p) → B/p ≅ D_{(d)}(A/p). Hence completed base change along α is conservative on derived (p, d)-complete objects, has finite (p, d)-complete Tor amplitude, and satisfies α̂^*∆_{R/A} ≅ ∆_{R_B/B} for p-completely smooth A/(d)-algebras R (Lemma 4.20). Composing with the universal oriented prism reduces the Hodge–Tate comparison for any bounded oriented prism to the characteristic-p case.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Construction 6.1 and the proof of Proposition 6.2, pp. 51–52
items.note: A homologically better-behaved refinement of the crude map A → W(A/d) of Remark 2.22. This is the device that transports the characteristic-p Hodge–Tate comparison to mixed characteristic. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the hypotheses of Construction 6.1 and the construction itself were stated. the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§4–6 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate comparison for the affine line
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. If R is the p-adic completion of the polynomial ring A/I⟨X⟩, then η⁰_R : R → H⁰(∆̄_{R/A}) and η¹_R{−1} : Ω¹_{R/(A/I)}{−1} → H¹(∆̄_{R/A}) are isomorphisms and H^i(∆̄_{R/A}) = 0 for i > 1. In particular Lemma 4.10 holds in general.
items.note: The base case, from which Theorem 6.3 follows by flat descent and base change. PR.1's acceptance list names 'smooth polynomial algebra, an étale chart, a crystalline base'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the standing hypothesis was added.

items.name: The de Rham comparison
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Assume W(A/I) is p-torsionfree (e.g. A/I p-torsionfree, or I = (p) with A/p reduced). Then there is a natural isomorphism ∆_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ} A/I ≅ Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} of commutative algebras in D(X_ét, A/I), with p-adic completion.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 6.4 and Theorem 1.8 (3), pp. 4 and 53
items.note: The Frobenius twist is essential and the statement is not the untwisted Hodge–Tate direct sum, a point PR.1 makes explicitly: 'Prove the de Rham comparison after phi_A-twisted reduction, with its completed tensor and differential; it is not the same as an untwisted Hodge–Tate direct sum.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the claim that it 'upgrades to an isomorphism of commutative differential graded algebras' is only asserted in Theorem 1.8(3); it follows by reducing the map φ̃ of Theorem 15.3 modulo I ([BMS1, Prop. 6.12]) and applying Theorem 4.11, but the paper does not write this out. The version without the hypothesis on W(A/I) (Corollary 15.4) was split off as item 37b.

items.name: The de Rham comparison in general
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. There is a canonical isomorphism of E_∞-algebras ∆_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ} A/I ≅ Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} in D(X_ét, A/I) [the paper prints Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}; sourceIssues E1]. It is proved by reducing the map φ̃ of Theorem 15.3 modulo I and using [BMS1, Prop. 6.12] and the Hodge–Tate comparison.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 37). PR.3 plans the Lη_I Frobenius factorization of §15 from which it follows, and PR.1 the de Rham comparison.

items.name: Semiperfectoid and quasiregular semiperfectoid rings
items.statement: A ring S is semiperfectoid if it is derived p-complete and a quotient of a perfectoid ring. It is quasiregular if in addition it has bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{S/ℤ_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S; such S are classically p-adically complete.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Notation 7.1 and Theorem 1.12, pp. 6 and 55, following [BMS19, §4.4]
items.note: Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings form a basis for the quasisyntomic topology, which is why they carry the whole descent strategy of §§12–15. DD.0 plans quasisyntomic maps and the cotangent criteria; PR.2 plans the discrete δ/prism calculation for quasiregular semiperfectoid inputs. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): DD.0 does not plan the semiperfectoid covers; DD.5 does ('prove existence/refinement of the semiperfectoid covers used by BMS2'), as in the accepted PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/035.

items.name: Universal prisms and universal perfectoidizations of semiperfectoid rings
items.statement: For S semiperfectoid, the category of prisms (A, I) with a map S → A/I has an initial object (∆^init_S, I) with I = (d) principal (Proposition 7.2). Letting (∆^init_S)_perf be the completed perfection and S_perfd = (∆^init_S)_perf/I, the ring S_perfd is perfectoid and S → S_perfd is the universal map from S to a perfectoid ring (Corollary 7.3). Moreover S → S_perfd is surjective (Theorem 7.4).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proposition 7.2, Corollary 7.3 and Theorem 7.4, and Theorem 1.12, pp. 6 and 55–56
items.note: Surjectivity is the striking point: it implies that Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed subsets of an affinoid perfectoid space agree, contrary to a claim in [Sch15, Remark II.2.4] (Remark 7.5), and it gives a good notion of almost mathematics with respect to any ideal of a perfectoid ring (Remark 1.13). Q2 plans the universal prism and the universal perfectoidization; Q4 plans Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5 explicitly. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Theorem 1.12(1) and the remark after Proposition 7.2 identify the category with the absolute prismatic site of Remark 4.7, which uses bounded prisms, whereas the initial prism is not bounded in general (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Derived prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Fix a bounded prism (A, I). Left Kan extend R ↦ ∆_{R/A} from p-completely smooth A/I-algebras to all derived p-complete simplicial commutative A/I-algebras. The Hodge–Tate comparison then gives ∆̄_{R/A} = ∆_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I an exhaustive increasing filtration with gr_i the derived p-completion of ∧^i L_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i]. Consequences: the functor is unchanged on p-completely smooth algebras; it is a sheaf for the p-completely étale topology, hence defined for p-adic formal schemes; for (A, I) perfect it is a sheaf for the quasisyntomic topology; its formation commutes with base change: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J), with R_B the derived p-completion of R ⊗^L_A B, one has ∆_{R_B/B} ≅ ∆_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B (derived (p, J)-completion). Finally, the functor ∆_{−/A}, from derived p-complete simplicial commutative A/I-algebras to (p, I)-complete E_∞-algebras in D(A), is symmetric monoidal and commutes with all colimits.
items.note: PR.2: 'Extend the smooth-algebra functor by the coherent left Kan extension of BS22 Construction 7.6 and derived completion. Prove independence and the filtered derived Hodge–Tate comparison with exterior powers of the completed cotangent complex.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): part (5) of Construction 7.6 (colimits and symmetric monoidality), which Lemma 8.6 and Proposition 8.13 use, and the exact base-change formula were added.

items.name: Derived prismatic cohomology when it is discrete
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra such that ∆̄_{R/A} = ∆_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is concentrated in degree 0. (1) The φ_A-linear Frobenius on ∆_{R/A} lifts naturally to a δ-A-structure on the ring ∆_{R/A}. (2) (∆_{R/A}, I∆_{R/A}) is a prism over (A, I) with a map R → ∆̄_{R/A}. (3) The category of prisms (B, J) over (A, I) with a map R → B/J has an initial object; (∆_{R/A}, I∆_{R/A}) is weakly initial, and the initial object is the image of an idempotent endomorphism of (∆_{R/A}, I∆_{R/A}). The authors conjecture that (∆_{R/A}, I∆_{R/A}) is itself initial.
items.note: Lemma 7.8 is the abstract idempotent-retract statement in an idempotent complete category. PR.2 names 'the discrete delta/prism calculation for quasiregular semiperfectoid inputs and the initial-prism comparison, including regular quotient and idempotent-retract arguments in BS22 §§7.7–7.10'. The conjecture in part (3) is recorded here as an open point. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the hypothesis is on ∆̄_{R/A}, not ∆_{R/A}, and the initial object is a retract of ∆_{R/A}, not conversely. Lemma 7.8 was made its own item (105).

items.name: Prismatic cohomology of an lci quotient
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R = A/J with J = (I, f₁,…,f_r) and f₁,…,f_r Koszul-regular on A/I, with R of bounded p-torsion. Then ∆_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0 and I-torsionfree, and (∆_{R/A}, I∆_{R/A}) is the initial object of (R/A)_∆; locally on Spf(A), where I = (d), it is the prismatic envelope A{f₁/d, …, f_r/d}^∧ of Proposition 3.13.
items.note: The computation that identifies the derived and the site-theoretic constructions in the regular case, and PR.2's acceptance example 'regular semiperfectoid quotient'.

items.name: The prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: Let S be quasiregular semiperfectoid, R any perfectoid ring mapping to S and (A, I) = (A_inf(R), ker θ). Then ∆̄_{S/A} is discrete (so ∆_{S/A} is discrete and I-torsionfree), and ∆_{S/A} is the initial prism ∆^init_S with its map S → ∆^init_S/I, independently of R, and S → ∆̄_{S/A} is p-completely faithfully flat. One writes ∆_S for this ring.
items.note: This is the object whose Nygaard filtration is computed in §12 and compared with π₀TP in §13. Planned by PR.2 and reexported by Q2. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the discreteness hypothesis of the proposition is on the reduced complex.

items.name: Lifting quasisyntomic covers to the prismatic site
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a quasisyntomic A/I-algebra. Then there is an object (B → B/IB ← R) of (R/A)_∆ with R → B/IB p-completely faithfully flat; hence (A, I) → (B, IB) is a flat map of prisms, faithfully flat if A/I → R is, and if A is perfect the same holds for the perfection (B, IB)_perf.
items.note: Together with Examples 7.12 and 7.13 this produces the perfectoid covers of the final object of the prismatic site, relative for R smooth and absolute for A/I regular, cited in Remark 4.5 for the theory of F-crystals [BS21]; Proposition 7.11 itself is used in Theorem 7.14 and in the proof of Theorem 15.2. Q3 plans 'the additional lifting theorem for quasisyntomic covers to bounded prisms, BS22 7.11'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the note had said the Example 7.12–7.13 covers are used throughout §§12–15; they are not (§§12–15 use the covers B → B̃ of §12.5). Examples 7.12 and 7.13 are now items 107 and 108.

items.name: André's flatness lemma
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. Then there is a p-completely faithfully flat map R → S of perfectoid rings with S absolutely integrally closed; in particular every element of S admits a compatible system of p-power roots. The map can moreover be chosen to be an ind-syntomic cover modulo p.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 7.14 and Remark 7.15, pp. 61–62
items.note: The prismatic proof: adjoin p-power roots of a root of a monic polynomial, lift to a prism by Proposition 7.11, perfect, and iterate transfinitely. It is the key input to Theorem 7.4, to §10 and to Theorem 14.1. Q3 plans exactly this: 'Prove Theorem 7.14 … Construct the extension by adjoining roots of monic polynomials, lifting to a prism, perfecting, and transfinite iteration.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the proof formally adjoins roots of all monic polynomials, applies Proposition 7.11(2) to get a perfect prism (B, IB) with R → B/IB p-completely faithfully flat, and iterates transfinitely.

items.name: The perfection of prismatic cohomology and the perfectoidization of an algebra
items.statement: Fix a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I) and a distinguished generator d. For a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S, set ∆_{S/A, perf} := (colim(∆_{S/A} →^φ φ_*∆_{S/A} →^φ φ²_*∆_{S/A} → …))^∧_{(p,I)}, a derived (p, I)-complete E_∞-A-algebra with a φ_A-semilinear automorphism, and S_perfd := ∆_{S/A, perf} ⊗^L_A A/I, a p-complete E_∞-S-algebra. Both are independent of A and depend only on π₀S.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Notation 8.1 and Definition 8.2, p. 63
items.note: For S of characteristic p this recovers the naive perfection S_perf (Example 8.3); in general ∆_{S/A,perf} and S_perfd lie in D^{≥0} (Lemma 8.4). PR.2: 'Construct perfect-prismatic/perfected cohomology separately and establish the comparison with the nonperfect theory rather than replacing one by the other.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the Frobenius pushforwards φ_* had been written φ^*. Example 8.3 (characteristic p) and Lemma 8.4 (coconnectivity) are items 109 and 110.

items.name: The perfect prismatic site computes the perfection
items.statement: For any topology on (S/A)_∆^perf between the flat and the chaotic one, the map ∆_{S/A, perf} → RΓ((S/A)_∆^perf, O_∆) is an equivalence; consequently S_perfd ≅ RΓ((S/A)_∆^perf, Ō_∆) ≅ lim_{S → R′} R′ is the derived limit over all maps from S to perfectoid rings, and is independent of A. For S semiperfectoid it agrees with the perfectoidization of Corollary 7.3.
items.note: This is the comparison PR.2 asks for between the perfected theory and the non-perfect one, and the reason perfectoidization can be studied by descent. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the status was planned at PR.2; it is missing. The proof uses Theorem 7.4 ('the composite is surjective') and André's lemma, Theorem 7.14, which are at PerfectoidQuotients Q4 and Q3; both lie downstream of PR.2, and PR.2 says 'These later Q theorems are not prerequisites'. It goes to the Part II of route 3 with the rest of the perfectoidization theory.

items.name: Descendability of the passage to the perfection
items.statement: Let T = R[X₁,…,X_n]^∧ and T_∞ = R[X₁^{1/p^∞},…,X_n^{1/p^∞}]^∧. Then ∆_{T/A} → ∆_{T_∞/A} and ∆_{T/A, perf} → ∆_{T_∞/A, perf} are descendable as maps of commutative algebras in D_comp(A), in the sense of Mathew.
items.note: Descendability — the property that the unit is a retract of a finite-stage totalization, giving uniform bounds on descent — is a general notion of Mathew's used here to control limits of perfectoidizations. It appears nowhere in the atlas: a text search of every stage description for 'descendability' returns nothing, and neither PR.2 nor PerfectoidSpaces mentions it, although PR.2 names BS22 §8 among its sources. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): descendability itself is not new to the atlas: the accepted route 6 of PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17 gives Mathew's definition, the index and [BS17, Lemma 11.22] (the lemma this proof cites) to EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract, and its reason says this item 'consumes this generic object in prismatic perfection; do not rebuild it in PR2'. What remains missing is Lemma 8.6 itself, a source of PR.2 that imports E5:abstract.

items.name: The arc-topology on p-adic formal schemes and the site of perfectoids
items.statement: On the category fSch of p-adic formal schemes, declare a map Y → X of qcqs objects to be an arc-cover if for every p-adically complete rank-one valuation ring V with a map Spf V → X there is a faithfully flat extension V ⊂ W of such rings and a lift Spf W → Y; the arc-site is generated by arc-covers and open covers. Let Perfd ⊂ fSch be the full subcategory of formal schemes locally of the form Spf R with R perfectoid, with the induced topology.
items.note: A text search of every stage description in the atlas for 'arc-topology', 'arc-descent' and 'arc cover' returns nothing; the only related material is the pro-étale and v-topologies of DiamondsAndVStacks D2, which are topologies on diamonds and v-stacks, not on p-adic formal schemes, and are not a substitute. PR.2 names BS22 §8 as a source but plans only the perfected-cohomology comparison. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the arc-topology has an accepted owner, the new roadmap ArcTopologyAndDescent of PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21 route 1 (also fed by accepted routes of PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24, PAPER-GUO-REINECKE-24, PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17 and PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21); this definition is its p-adic variant arc_p, and it moves there (route 2).

items.name: Perfectoids form a basis for the arc-topology and the structure sheaf is an arc-sheaf on them
items.statement: Every p-adic formal scheme admits an arc-cover by an object of Perfd (Lemma 8.8); indeed any p-complete ring admits a p-complete arc-cover by a product of p-complete rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field (Remark 8.9). The presheaf O on Perfd is an arc-sheaf with H^i_arc(Spf R, O) = 0 for i > 0 when R is perfectoid, and X ↦ Hom(X, T) is an arc-sheaf on Perfd for every p-adic formal scheme T (Proposition 8.10).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 8.8, Remark 8.9 and Proposition 8.10, p. 67
items.note: The structure sheaf is emphatically not an arc-sheaf on all of fSch — nilpotents are invisible to valuation rings — so the restriction to Perfd is essential. The proof of Proposition 8.10 uses arc-descent for perfect schemes and, for the representability statement, an argument of Gabber together with approximation by finite-type F_p-schemes. Not planned anywhere in the atlas. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the paper proves 8.8–8.10 itself but imports from Bhatt–Mathew the arc-covers of schemes [BM18, Def. 1.2] and the exactness of the Čech complex of an arc-cover of perfect schemes ([BS17, Thm 4.1], [BM18, Thm 1.6], [BS17, Lemma 6.3]); for the Hom(−, T) part it uses Gabber's argument ([Bha16, Rem. 4.6], Stacks 03K0), [TT90, App. C], and the uncited fact that arc-covers of perfections of finite-type F_p-schemes are h-covers. Footnote 11 says the v-topology would suffice for the applications. The imported inputs are item 112. Moved to route 2 (ArcTopologyAndDescent).

items.name: Perfectoidization is arc-descent
items.statement: For any p-complete ring S one has S_perfd = RΓ_arc(Spf S, O); in particular S ↦ S_perfd satisfies descent for the arc-topology.
items.note: The formula that turns perfectoidization into a cohomological invariant and makes §10 possible. It is not planned by any layer: the atlas's perfectoidization statements are Q2's universal property and Q4's surjectivity, neither of which mentions the arc-topology. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): moved to the Part II of route 3.

items.name: The excision pullback square for perfectoidization
items.statement: Let S → S′ be a map of derived p-complete rings and I ⊂ S a derived p-complete ideal such that, for every p-complete rank-one valuation ring V and every map S → V not killing I, there is a unique extension to S′ → V (for example, if S → S′ is integral and Spec S′ → Spec S is an isomorphism outside V(I)). Then the square with corners S_perfd, S′_perfd, (S/I)_perfd, (S′/I)_perfd is a pullback square of E_∞-S-algebras. In particular, if S and S′ are perfectoid, the kernel and cokernel of S → S′ are killed by ker(S → (S/I)_perfd).
items.note: Corollary 8.12 is the excision property that drives the proof of Theorem 10.11. None of these is planned: PR.2 and Q2 plan the construction and universal property of perfectoidization, not its arc-descent, excision or monoidality. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split: Proposition 8.13 is item 52b and Corollary 8.14 item 52c. The hypothesis was stated as in the paper, and the note's claim that the corollary is 'the only tool' controlling such maps is not the paper's.

items.name: Perfectoidization is symmetric monoidal
items.statement: The functor S ↦ S_perfd, from derived p-complete simplicial rings admitting a map from a perfectoid ring to derived p-complete E_∞-rings, is symmetric monoidal: for S₁ ← S₃ → S₂ the map S_{1,perfd} ⊗̂^L_{S_{3,perfd}} S_{2,perfd} → (S₁ ⊗̂^L_{S₃} S₂)_perfd is an equivalence.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 52). Its proof uses only derived prismatic cohomology (Construction 7.6(5)), so it belongs with PR.2's perfected cohomology (route 1).

items.name: Connective perfectoidizations are perfectoid
items.statement: Let S be a derived p-complete simplicial ring admitting a map from a perfectoid ring. If S_perfd is connective (equivalently, by Lemma 8.4, concentrated in degree 0), then S_perfd is a perfectoid ring and S → S_perfd is the universal map to a perfectoid ring.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 52). Route 1 (PR.2), with Proposition 8.13.

items.name: The étale comparison theorem
items.statement: Fix a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, (d)) and a p-adic formal scheme X over R, with adic generic fibre X_η = X ×_{Spf R} Spa(R[1/p], R) and nearby-cycles map µ : X_{η,ét} → X_ét. Then Rµ_*ℤ/pⁿ ≅ (∆_{X/A}[1/d]/pⁿ)^{φ=1}; in particular for X = Spf(S) affine, RΓ(Spec(S[1/p]), ℤ/pⁿ) ≅ (∆_{S/A}[1/d]/pⁿ)^{φ=1}. There are no restrictions on the singularities of X. Without inverting p or d one has ℤ/pⁿ ≅ (∆_{X/A}/pⁿ)^{φ=1} as étale sheaves (Remark 9.3).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 9.1, Remark 9.3 and Theorem 1.8 (4), pp. 4 and 71–73
items.note: The proof rests on Lemma 9.2, that on derived t-complete objects the functors M ↦ M^{φ=1} and M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1} commute with colimits, plus arc-descent for the two sides. PR.4: 'For a perfect base prism and the smooth formal scheme of BS22 §9, construct the comparison from generic-fiber Z/p^n étale cohomology to (Δ/p^n[1/I])^(phi=1). Define phi=1 as a derived fixed-point/fiber construction, not fixed vectors in H^0.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the status was planned at PR.4; it is missing. PR.4 plans the comparison only 'for a perfect base prism and the smooth formal scheme of BS22 §9', while the theorem has 'no restrictions on the singularities of X'. The proof also uses the arc_p-topology and arc_p-descent of Bhatt–Mathew (item 112), Corollary 8.11 (item 51), Remark 8.9, Example 8.3, and [Hub96, Cor. 3.2.2] with [Sch12, Thm 1.11] (item 113); Remark 9.3 is left to the reader. Routed as a source of PR.4 (route 1), which must import ArcTopologyAndDescent and the Part II of route 3.

items.name: Fixed points commute with completed colimits
items.statement: Let B be an F_p-algebra with t ∈ B, and let D_comp(B[F]) be the ∞-category of pairs (M, φ : M → φ_*M) with M derived t-complete. Then M ↦ M^{φ=1} and M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1} commute with colimits.
items.note: Described by the authors as slightly surprising; it is what allows the étale comparison to be checked arc-locally. Planned as part of PR.4's φ=1 construction. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): φ_* had been printed φ^* in the item.

items.name: p-adic Tate twists of a perfectoid ring
items.statement: For a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, (d)) one has ℤ_p(n)(R) ≅ fib(φ^{-1}(d)ⁿA →^{φ/dⁿ − 1} A). For n ≥ 1 there is a canonical identification ℤ_p(n)(R) ≅ RΓ(Spec(R[1/p]), ℤ_p(n)); for n = 0, ℤ_p(0)(R) ≅ RΓ(Spec(R), ℤ_p) ≅ RΓ(Spec((R/p)_perf), ℤ_p).
items.note: The bridge between the syntomic ℤ_p(n) of [BMS19] and ordinary Tate twists on the generic fibre. Remark 9.5 explains that the construction of the comparison map for n = 1 uses the cyclotomic trace, and that a purely algebraic prismatic logarithm giving the same map is constructed in Bhatt–Lurie. PR.4 plans the syntomic Tate twists and names BS22 §9 as a source. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): for n = 0 the paper leaves the details to the reader (via Remark 9.3 and Gabber's affine proper base change).

items.name: Picard groups of perfectoid rings are uniquely p-divisible
items.statement: For a quasisyntomic ring R one has Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≅ ℤ_p(1)(R), where Pic(R) = τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m)[1] and the completion is p-adic (Lemma 9.6). Consequently, for a perfectoid ring R, both Pic(R) and Pic(R[1/p]) are uniquely p-divisible (Corollary 9.7).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 9.6 and Corollary 9.7, p. 76
items.note: Used in §14 to identify H¹(ℤ_p(1)(R)) with H⁰ of the derived p-completion of R^*. Part of §9, which PR.4 names as a source. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): PR.4 plans 'descent, perfectoid local calculations', which covers Corollary 9.7. Lemma 9.6 restates [BMS2, Prop. 7.17], which the accepted PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/066 routes to RefinedTraceMethods RT.6, and Corollary 9.7 uses p-complete arc-descent (ArcTopologyAndDescent); PR.4 imports both (RT.6 is not downstream of PR.4).

items.name: Almost mathematics with respect to an arbitrary finitely generated ideal of a perfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring and J ⊂ R a derived p-complete ideal, and set J_perfd := ker(R → (R/J)_perfd). A derived p-complete R-module M is J-almost zero if J_perfd M = 0. The J-almost zero derived p-complete modules are stable under kernels, cokernels and extensions and form a ⊗-ideal equivalent to the category of derived p-complete (R/J)_perfd-modules (Proposition 10.2); the multiplication maps J_perfd ⊗̂^L_R J_perfd → J_perfd and (R/J)_perfd ⊗̂^L_R (R/J)_perfd → (R/J)_perfd are quasi-isomorphisms and J_perfd ⊗̂^L_R (R/J)_perfd = 0 (Lemma 10.3). A derived p-complete complex M is J-almost zero if and only if J_perfd ⊗̂^L_R M = 0, and such complexes form a thick tensor ideal (Proposition 10.4).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 10.1 and Propositions 10.2, 10.4, Lemma 10.3, pp. 78–79
items.note: For J = (p) one recovers the usual almost mathematics of a perfectoid ring, since J_perfd is then the ideal of p-power roots of p. Remark 1.13 advertises this as one of the paper's contributions: the surjectivity of S → S_perfd gives a good almost setting for any closed subset, not only for the ideal of p-power roots of p. PerfectoidSpaces P0 plans almost mathematics 'with a reusable base ideal' but instantiates it in P1–P2 only with fractional powers of a pseudouniformizer; the identification of the J-almost category with derived p-complete (R/J)_perfd-modules is specific to this paper and is planned nowhere. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): finite generation is assumed only in Theorem 10.9 (Remark 1.13 says 'any p-complete ideal'). For J = (p) one has J_perfd = √(pR). Moved to the Part II of route 3.

items.name: A connectivity criterion for almost-connective complexes
items.statement: A p-complete complex M ∈ D(R) is connective if and only if M ⊗̂^L_R R/J_perfd is connective and M is J-almost connective, i.e. H^i(M) is J-almost zero for i > 0.
items.note: The device that upgrades an almost statement to an honest one, and hence upgrades the almost version of Theorem 10.9 to Theorem 10.11 and then back to Theorem 10.9 in general. Not planned by any layer. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): moved to the Part II of route 3.

items.name: J-almost Galois extensions
items.statement: A p-complete R-algebra S with an action of a finite group G is a J-almost G-Galois extension if R → RΓ(G, S) and S ⊗̂^L_R S → ∏_G S are J-almost isomorphisms (Definition 10.6).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 10.6 and Remark 10.7, p. 79
items.note: The almost setting (R/pⁿ, J_{perfd,n}) is a basic setup in the sense of Gabber–Ramero, and the paper notes that André's standing flatness assumption on m ⊗ m is not needed for his Proposition 1.9.1. None of this is planned: PerfectoidSpaces P0 builds almost algebra for an abstract idempotent base ideal but does not treat almost Galois covers. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Proposition 10.8 was split off as item 59b.

items.name: Almost Galois covers are almost finite projective
items.statement: If S is a J-almost G-Galois extension of R, then for all n > 0 the map R/pⁿ → S/pⁿ is almost finite projective and almost unramified with respect to the almost setting (R/pⁿ, J_{perfd,n}). More generally, if for a subgroup H ⊂ G the map S′ = S^H → S is a J-almost H-Galois cover, then R/pⁿ → S′/pⁿ is almost finite projective and almost unramified.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 59). André's Proposition 1.9.1 in an abstract almost setting; the paper notes that André's flatness assumption on m ⊗ m is not needed. It is general almost algebra over a basic setup, which PerfectoidSpaces P0 builds, so it is a source of P0 (route 6).

items.name: The almost purity theorem for integral algebras over a perfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring, J ⊂ R a finitely generated ideal and S a finitely presented finite R-algebra such that Spec(S) → Spec(R) is finite étale outside V(J). Then S_perfd is discrete and perfectoid, S → S_perfd is an isomorphism away from V(J), and for n > 0 the map R/pⁿ → S_perfd/pⁿ is almost finite projective and almost unramified for the almost setting (R/pⁿ, J_{perfd,n}). If S carries a G-action which is G-Galois outside V(J), then R → S_perfd is a J-almost G-Galois cover.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 10.9 and Theorem 1.17 (2), pp. 9 and 80–81
items.note: This reduces to the classical almost purity theorem when J = (p) and improves the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma of André when J = (g); the proof avoids adic spaces and perfectoid spaces entirely, so it is a new proof of both (Remark 10.10). The key inputs are the arc-descent properties of perfectoidization, in particular Corollary 8.12, and André's flatness lemma. PerfectoidSpaces P3 plans almost purity only for perfectoid Tate rings in the form of ECD Theorem 6.1, by the Scholze/Kedlaya–Liu route, and explicitly for the ideal of fractional powers of a pseudouniformizer; the statement here is stronger and its proof is different. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): moved to the Part II of route 3.

items.name: Perfectoidization of an integral algebra over a perfectoid ring is discrete
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, I) and let R → S be the p-completion of an integral map. Then ∆_{S/A, perf} is discrete and a perfect p-complete δ-A-algebra; consequently S_perfd is discrete and perfectoid, and S → S_perfd is the universal map from S to a perfectoid ring.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 10.11 and Theorem 1.17 (1), pp. 9 and 82
items.note: The general form of the perfectoidization theorem: Corollary 7.3 covers semiperfectoid quotients, while this covers arbitrary integral algebras. The proof is an induction along the constructible stratification of Lemma 10.12, using Corollary 8.12 for excision and the almost form of Theorem 10.9. PerfectoidQuotients Q2 and Q4 plan the semiperfectoid case and its surjectivity but not the integral case. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): moved to the Part II of route 3.

items.name: Finite maps are finite étale over a constructible stratification, up to universal homeomorphisms
items.statement: Let R → S be a finitely presented finite map of ℤ_(p)-algebras. Then there are g₁,…,g_n ∈ R generating the unit ideal such that, setting R_i = R/(g₁,…,g_{i−1})_red[1/g_i] and S_i likewise, each R_i → S_i factors as R_i → T_i → S_i with R_i → T_i finite étale, T_i → S_i a universal homeomorphism which is an isomorphism after inverting p, and with p either zero or invertible in each R_i.
items.note: The commutative-algebra input to the proof of Theorem 10.11 ('We needed the following lemma'), which stratifies the base so that the inductive proof of Theorem 10.11 can run. Not planned by any layer of the atlas. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): moved to the Part II of route 3.

items.name: An almost-vanishing consequence for absolute integral closures
items.statement: For R a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic and R → S a finite extension inside an absolute integral closure R⁺, and any n > 0, there is c ∈ pR — any c with R[1/c] → S[1/c] finite étale will do — such that Tor_i^{R/pⁿ}(S/pⁿ, −) → Tor_i^{R/pⁿ}(R⁺/pⁿ, −) is c-almost zero for all i > 0, i.e. its image is annihilated by all p-power roots c^{1/p^m} ∈ R⁺ of c.
items.note: A quick reproof of [HM17, Theorem 1.3] (Heitmann–Ma, Extended plus closure in complete local rings, arXiv:1708.05761; 'the main theorems of [HM17] follow almost immediately') from Theorem 10.9, using the perfectoid cover of Remark 3.11. It is recorded here because it shows the intended downstream use of the almost purity theorem in commutative algebra. Not planned by any layer. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the result reproved is Heitmann–Ma's, not Hochster–Ma's; the prerequisite entry and route 3's reason had the same misattribution. Moved to the Part II of route 3.

items.name: The étale cohomological dimension of a perfectoid ring
items.statement: For a perfectoid ring R the F_p-étale cohomological dimension of X = Spec(R[1/p]) is at most 1: for every étale F_p-sheaf F on X one has H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > 1. Here X is the scheme, not the adic spectrum; the statement fails for general sheaves on the adic spectrum.
items.note: Proved from Theorems 9.1, 10.11 and 7.4: reduce to j_!F_p on Y = Spec S[1/p] for S finitely presented and finite over R; by Theorem 9.1 for S and S/J, RΓ(Y, j_!F_p) is (−/p[1/I])^{φ=1} of fib(∆_{S/A,perf} → ∆_{(S/J)/A,perf}), which is connective because S_perfd and (S/J)_perfd are discrete perfectoid (Theorem 10.11) and S_perfd → (S/J)_perfd is surjective (Theorem 7.4). PR.4 names BS22 §11 as one of its sources. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): PR.4 lists BS22 §11 among its sources; its blueprint must import Theorem 10.11 from the Part II of route 3 (an edge the Part II's brief records) and Theorem 7.4 from Q4, which is upstream of PR.4.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration on the prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfectoid with prism (∆_S, (d)), set Fil^i_N ∆_S = {x ∈ ∆_S : φ(x) ∈ d^i ∆_S}. This is an N-indexed decreasing multiplicative filtration, in general not separated.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 12.1 and Theorem 1.14 (2), pp. 7 and 86
items.note: PR.3: 'On the discrete quasiregular semiperfectoid calculation construct Nygaard pieces by the actual Frobenius-divisibility condition', and it warns that 'Nygaard completion of Δ is not silently identified with Δ in all contexts'.

items.name: The Nygaard and conjugate filtrations correspond
items.statement: Let S be quasiregular semiperfectoid, R a perfectoid ring mapping to S with perfect prism (A, (d)), so that ∆̄_S carries the conjugate filtration with gr_i ∆̄_S = (∧^i L_{S/R}[−i])^∧. Then the image of Fil^i_N ∆_S under φ/d^i : ∆_S → ∆̄_S is Fil_i ∆̄_S, giving a natural isomorphism gr^i_N ∆_S ≅ Fil_i ∆̄_S{i}.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 12.2 and Theorem 1.14, pp. 7 and 86
items.note: The conjugate filtration genuinely depends on the choice of R: Example 12.3 exhibits S = O_{C_p} ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} O_{C_p} with two different conjugate filtrations, distinguished by a Galois-equivariance argument using Tate's computation of RΓ(Γ, R{1}).
