PR.3 plans 'the associated-graded description, comparison with Hodge–Tate and de Rham filtrations'.

items.name: The explicit q-divided-power computation in the model case
items.statement: Let R = ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ with perfect prism (A, ([p]_q)), A the (p, [p]_q)-completion of ℤ_p[q^{1/p^∞}], and S = (ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}][X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧. Then ∆_S = A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/[p]_q}^∧ with δ(q) = δ(Y) = 0 and X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ ∆_S for all n, and ∆_S is the (p, [p]_q)-completion of ⊕_{i∈ℕ[1/p]} A·Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q! (Lemma 12.4). Fil^n_N ∆_S is the completion of ⊕_i [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{n−⌊i⌋}·A·Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!, the power read as 1 for i ≥ n + 1; the image of φ/[p]_q^n in ∆̄_S = (⊕_i ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}]·Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!)^∧ and Fil_n ∆̄_S are both the summands with i < p(n+1), so Theorem 12.2 holds for S (Lemma 12.7). The inputs: if D is a (p, [p]_q)-completely flat ℤ_p⟦q−1⟧-algebra with φ : D → D and x ∈ D with φ(q) = q^p, φ(x) = x^p and φ(x) ∈ [p]_qD, then x^n ∈ [n]_q!D for all n ≥ 0 (Lemma 12.5); and in ℤ_p⟦q−1⟧, [mp]_q! = u·φ([m]_q!)·[p]_q^m and [⌊i⌋p]_q! = [⌊ip⌋]_q!·v for i ∈ ℕ[1/p], with u, v units (Lemma 12.6).
items.note: The explicit base case from which the general theorem is bootstrapped, via the p-completely regular quotient case (Proposition 12.8) and then quasisyntomic descent and left Kan extension (Definition 12.9, Propositions 12.10 and 12.11). Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the coefficient in the Nygaard filtration is [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{n−⌊i⌋} = φ^{−1}([p]_q)^{n−⌊i⌋}, not [p]_q^{(n−⌊i⌋)/p}, and the base R and the hypotheses of Lemma 12.5 were missing.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration by descent and by left Kan extension agree
items.statement: Let R be perfectoid with perfect prism (A, (d)) and B a p-completely smooth R-algebra. For a surjection R⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ → B let B̃ = R⟨X₁^{1/p^∞},…,X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗_{R⟨X⟩} B, with Čech nerve B̃^•; ∆_{B̃^•} computes ∆_{B/A}. Fil^i_N ∆_{B/A} is the totalization of Fil^i_N ∆_{B̃^•} ⊂ ∆_{B̃^•} (Definition 12.9). There is a natural map φ/d^i : Fil^i_N ∆_{B/A} → ∆_{B/A} projecting to an isomorphism gr^i_N ∆_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤i}∆̄_{B/A}, independent of the surjection [the paper prints τ^{≤i}∆_{B/A}; sourceIssues E23] (Proposition 12.10). The left Kan extension Fil^i_{N′} has gr^i_{N′} ≅ Fil_i ∆̄; for S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Fil^i_{N′}∆_S is in degree 0 and equals Fil^i_N ∆_S, and Theorem 12.2 holds (Proposition 12.11).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 12.9, Propositions 12.10 and 12.11, pp. 92–93
items.note: PR.3: 'Extend them by the proved quasisyntomic descent and use the appropriate Frobenius-twisted relative complex for the relative filtration.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the resolution is the Čech nerve of B → B̃, not a Čech–Alexander resolution, and the hypotheses were missing.

items.name: The δ-ring structure on π₀TP and the Nygaard completion
items.statement: There is a functorial δ-ring structure on ∆̂_S = π₀TP(S; ℤ_p) for S quasiregular semiperfectoid, and the induced map ∆_S = ∆^init_S → ∆̂_S identifies ∆̂_S with the Nygaard completion of ∆_S, compatibly with Nygaard filtrations. In particular the cyclotomic Frobenius of topological Hochschild theory is the Frobenius lift attached to a δ-structure.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 13.1 and Theorem 1.14 (3), Remark 1.15, pp. 7–8 and 94–95
items.note: The authors call their proof very indirect and say they know no conceptual reason for it in terms of topological Hochschild homology. Lemma 13.2 is the technical statement δ(Fil^i_N) ⊂ Fil^{pi}_N + (d,p)^{i−1}. PR.3 assigns the trace-theoretic half to RefinedTraceMethods, which 'proves that BMS2's TC/THH filtration has these graded pieces in its source range, including comparison with the Nygaard-completed prismatic object'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the trace-theoretic half is RT.6's ('Also own the BMS2 quasisyntomic THH/TC⁻/TP computation and motivic-filtration interface … This stage constructs the trace-to-prismatic comparison'), not RT.3's, which is the Dennis/cyclotomic trace. Lemma 13.2 was split off as item 69b.

items.name: The δ-structure extends to the Nygaard completion
items.statement: Let S be quasiregular semiperfectoid. (1) δ(Fil^i_N ∆_S) ⊂ Fil^{pi}_N ∆_S + (d, p)^{i−1}∆_S. (2) The completion of ∆_S along {Fil^i_N ∆_S} equals its completion along {Fil^i_N ∆_S + (d, p)^j ∆_S}. Hence the δ-structure extends uniquely and continuously to the Nygaard completion.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 69). PR.3: 'State and prove the exact completeness/exhaustiveness assertions; Nygaard completion of Δ is not silently identified with Δ in all contexts'.

items.name: The p-adic Tate twists are discrete and torsionfree
items.statement: For each n ≥ 0 the quasisyntomic sheaf ℤ_p(n) of [BMS19] is discrete and p-torsionfree, resolving [BMS19, Conjecture 7.18].
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 14.1 and Theorem 1.18, pp. 9 and 97
items.note: The proof uses André's flatness lemma to reduce to a nice class of quasisyntomic rings, the explicit §12.2 computation, and the surjectivity statements of Lemmas 14.4 and 14.5; the K-theoretic consequence goes through the [BMS19] motivic filtration on TC and the identification of K-theory with TC of [CMM18]. It gives, for instance, that π_*K(O_C/pⁿ; ℤ_p) is concentrated in even degrees. PR.4 names BS22 §14 among its sources and owns the syntomic realization shared with RefinedTraceMethods. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 (the K-theoretic consequences) were split off as item 70b, which is missing. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Kept as planned at PR.4 ('Construct the syntomic/Tate-twist fibers … Prove the stated truncation'; Sources: BS22 §14), as in the accepted PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/068, and at RT.6 for the trace side. The proof uses Theorem 13.1 (RT.6, which is not downstream of PR.4), Theorem 9.4, Corollary 9.7, Lemmas 14.4–14.5 and André's lemma (Q3).

items.name: Evenness of p-adic and mod p K-theory
items.statement: Locally on the quasisyntomic site of any quasisyntomic ℤ_p-algebra, K(−; ℤ_p) and K(−)/p are concentrated in even degrees (Corollary 14.2, Theorem 1.18). If R is a perfectoid ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra and S = R/(f₁,…,f_r) for a regular sequence of elements admitting compatible p-power roots, then π_*K(R; ℤ_p) → π_*K(S; ℤ_p) is surjective in odd degrees, so evenness is inherited; for instance π_*K(O_C/pⁿ; ℤ_p) vanishes in odd degrees (Corollary 14.3).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 and Theorem 1.18, pp. 9 and 97–98
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 70). Not planned: it needs K ≃ τ_{≥0}TC for rings henselian along p with semiperfect reduction (item 95b), which the accepted Part II RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs owns, and RT.6's motivic filtration. Routed to that Part II (route 4).

items.name: Surjectivity statements for Tate twists and prisms of quotients
items.statement: (Lemma 14.4) Let R be a perfectoid ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra, R′ = R⟨X₁^{1/p^∞}, …, X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R′/(X₁, …, X_r). Then ℤ_p(n)(R′) → ℤ_p(n)(S) is surjective on H¹. (Lemma 14.5) Let R be any perfectoid ring. If S′ → S is a surjection of quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras such that the p-completion of L_{S′/R} → L_{S/R} is surjective on H^{−1}, then ∆_{S′} → ∆_S is surjective (by the Hodge–Tate comparison).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemmas 14.4 and 14.5, pp. 97 and 100
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Lemma 14.5 holds for any perfectoid R, not only ℤ_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebras, and the note misplaced the n = 0, 1 arguments: the lemmas are the two reduction steps of the proof of Theorem 14.1 (from S to S₀ by 14.5, and from S₀ to R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩ by 14.4), and the perfectoid case uses Theorem 9.4 with Artin–Schreier theory for n = 0 and Kummer theory, [BMS19, Prop. 7.17], Corollary 9.7 and André's lemma for n ≥ 1.

items.name: Large quasisyntomic algebras
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. A quasisyntomic A/I-algebra S (p-completely flat, derived p-complete, with L_{S/(A/I)} of p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]) is large if it admits a surjection from A/I⟨X_t^{1/p^∞} : t ∈ T⟩ for some set T. For such S, L_{S/(A/I)}[−1] is p-completely flat, and large algebras form a basis for the quasisyntomic site of A/I; examples are A/I⟨X₁^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f₁, …, f_m) with f₁, …, f_m p-completely regular relative to A/I.
items.note: The relative analogue of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings, which is what makes the relative Nygaard filtration descend. Planned by PR.3 and DD.5. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the bounded prism and the meaning of quasisyntomic were added, and the paper's index set I, which clashes with the ideal, was renamed T. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): DD.5 does not mention large algebras. PR.3 lists BS22 §§12–15 among its sources and asks for 'the appropriate Frobenius-twisted relative complex for the relative filtration', which is what large algebras are for; the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §15 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: Prismatic cohomology and the Nygaard filtration for large quasisyntomic algebras
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. For S a large quasisyntomic A/I-algebra, ∆_{S/A} is concentrated in degree 0 and (p, I)-completely flat over A, and is the initial object of (S/A)_∆. With φ_{S/A} : ∆^{(1)}_{S/A} := ∆_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ} A → ∆_{S/A} the relative Frobenius and Fil^i_N ∆^{(1)}_{S/A} = {x : φ_{S/A}(x) ∈ I^i ∆_{S/A}}, the image of gr^i_N under φ_{S/A} is Fil_i ∆̄_{S/A}{i}, and the formation of Fil^i_N commutes with base change in A.
items.note: The relative Nygaard filtration is on the Frobenius twist, a point PR.3 makes explicitly: 'use the appropriate Frobenius-twisted relative complex for the relative filtration'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the bounded prism was added.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration in the smooth case and the Frobenius isogeny
items.statement: On X_qsyn there is a sheaf ∆_{−/A} of (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebras, with Fil^i_N ∆^{(1)}_{−/A} = {x : φ(x) ∈ I^i∆_{−/A}} (Theorem 1.16 (1)). Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X = Spf(R) affine smooth over A/I. Then RΓ_∆(X/A) ≅ RΓ(X_qsyn, ∆_{−/A}); endowing it with Fil^i_N RΓ_∆(X/A)^{(1)} := RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N ∆^{(1)}_{−/A}) gives gr^i_N RΓ_∆(X/A)^{(1)} ≅ τ^{≤i}∆̄_{R/A}{i} for all i ≥ 0; and the Frobenius factors as φ^*_A RΓ_∆(X/A) →^{φ̃} Lη_I RΓ_∆(X/A) → RΓ_∆(X/A) with φ̃ an isomorphism.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 15.3 and Theorem 1.16, pp. 8 and 103
items.note: The décalage factorization is the prismatic form of the statement that Frobenius is an isogeny. PR.3: 'Prove the associated-graded description, comparison with Hodge–Tate and de Rham filtrations, and the Lη_I Frobenius factorization in BS22 §15. Use AI.1's generic Lη, independent of the AΩ construction.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Theorem 1.16 (1) was added.

items.name: The image of the Frobenius and the divided Frobenius maps V_i
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth formal A/I-scheme. The linearization φ_A^*RΓ_∆(X/A) → RΓ_∆(X/A) becomes an isomorphism after inverting I. More precisely, for each i ≥ 0 there is a natural map V_i : τ^{≤i}∆_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗i} → τ^{≤i}∆^{(1)}_{X/A} such that φ∘V_i is the natural map τ^{≤i}∆_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗i} → τ^{≤i}∆_{X/A} and V_i∘(φ ⊗ 1) : τ^{≤i}∆^{(1)}_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗i} → τ^{≤i}∆^{(1)}_{X/A} is the natural map. On H^i, V_i : H^i_∆(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗i} → H^i(X_ét, ∆^{(1)}_{X/A}) inverts φ up to I^{⊗i} [the paper's last display swaps source and target; sourceIssues E25]. If I = (d), V_i : H^i_∆(X/A) → H^i(φ_A^*RΓ_∆(X/A)) with V_iφ = φV_i = d^i.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Corollary 15.5 and Theorem 1.8 (6), pp. 5 and 104
items.note: PR.3: 'Construct divided Frobenius, inclusion/canonical maps, and BK twists by descent when I is not oriented.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item had the direction of V_i reversed and bars the paper does not have. It follows from φ̃ : ∆^{(1)} ≃ Lη_I∆ and [BMS18, Lemma 6.9].

items.name: Breuil–Kisin cohomology as prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Let K/ℚ_p be complete discretely valued with perfect residue field k and uniformizer π, 𝔖 = W(k)⟦u⟧ → O_K (u ↦ π) with kernel I. For any quasiregular semiperfectoid quasisyntomic O_K-algebra S, the cyclotomic Frobenius on π₀TP(S/𝕊[u]; ℤ_p) (topological Hochschild homology relative to the spherical polynomial ring 𝕊[u]) refines to a δ-ring structure, functorial in S, and identifies it with the Nygaard completion of ∆^{(1)}_{S/𝔖}, compatibly with Nygaard filtrations. Consequently, for i ≥ dim X, φ induces RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N of the completed ∆^{(1)}) ≅ RΓ(X_qsyn, ∆_{−/𝔖}) ⊗ I^{⊗i}, and with [BMS19, Prop. 11.5] RΓ_𝔖(X) ≅ RΓ_∆(X/𝔖).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proposition 15.7 and Example 1.9 (3), pp. 5–6 and 105
items.note: This is the comparison with [BMS19] which recovers all of its results on Breuil–Kisin cohomology. PR.3 assigns the trace-theoretic half to RefinedTraceMethods; AI.7 owns the cohomological Breuil–Kisin descent interface. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the relative THH is over the sphere-spectrum polynomial ring 𝕊[u], not 𝔖[u], and the setup was missing.

items.name: q-divided powers and q-PD pairs
items.statement: Let A = ℤ_p⟦q−1⟧ with δ(q) = 0 and [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1). For x in a [p]_q-torsionfree δ-A-algebra D with φ(x) ∈ [p]_q D, set γ(x) := φ(x)/[p]_q − δ(x), the divided [p]_q-th power. A q-PD pair is a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete δ-pair (D, I) over (A, (q−1)) such that φ(I) ⊂ [p]_q D and γ(I) ⊂ I, such that (D, ([p]_q)) is a bounded prism over (A, ([p]_q)), and such that D/(q−1) is p-torsionfree of finite (p, [p]_q)-complete Tor amplitude over D. If q − 1 = 0 in D one calls (D, I) a δ-PD pair; these are exactly the pairs with D p-torsionfree, D and I p-adically complete, and I admitting divided powers (x^n/n! ∈ I for x ∈ I, n > 0) (Remark 16.3). For a q-PD pair (D, I), (D/(q−1), ID/(q−1)) is a δ-PD pair, and this is left adjoint to the inclusion of δ-PD pairs into q-PD pairs (Remark 16.4).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Notation 16.1, Definition 16.2 and Remarks 16.3, 16.4, pp. 106–107
items.note: Being a q-PD pair is a property of a δ-pair, not extra structure, unlike the classical crystalline theory. PR.6: 'Construct q-PD pairs, q-crystalline envelopes and the q-crystalline site of BS22 §16.'

items.name: Homological and formal properties of q-PD pairs
items.statement: For a q-PD pair (D, I): D is derived f-complete for every f ∈ I; completed base change along D → D/(q−1) is conservative on (p, [p]_q)-complete complexes and commutes with totalizations of cosimplicial objects in D^{≥0}; the derived completion of I and the extension along a (p, [p]_q)-completely flat map of δ-A-algebras again give q-PD pairs (Lemma 16.5). The operation γ satisfies γ(x+y) = γ(x) + γ(y) + ((x+y)^p − x^p − y^p)/p and γ(fx) = φ(f)γ(x) − x^p δ(f), so the set of x in an ideal I with φ(x) ∈ [p]_qD and γ(x) ∈ I is an ideal (Remark 16.6); and, for D a [p]_q-torsionfree δ-A-algebra, φ^{-1}([p]_qD) is stable under γ (Lemma 16.7). Hence, for D a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete δ-A-algebra satisfying (2) and (3) of Definition 16.2, (q−1) is the smallest and φ^{-1}([p]_qD) the largest q-PD ideal of D (Corollary 16.8; the paper prints 'A-algebra', sourceIssues E27).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 16.5, Remark 16.6, Lemma 16.7 and Corollary 16.8, pp. 107–109
items.note: The additivity and multiplicativity formulas for γ are the q-analogues of the classical divided-power identities and are what make the q-PD condition checkable on generators. Planned by PR.6.

items.name: Examples and envelopes of q-PD pairs
items.statement: The key examples are (A, (q−1)), which is initial, and more generally (D, (q−1)) for D a (p,[p]_q)-completely flat A-algebra; the perfect object (A_inf, (ξ)) with ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q); and the classical case of a p-torsionfree p-complete δ-ring with an ideal admitting divided powers (Example 16.9). Given a q-PD pair (D, I), a (p,[p]_q)-completely flat δ-D-algebra P and a sequence x₁,…,x_r ∈ P that is (p,[p]_q)-completely regular relative to D, the algebra E := P{φ(x₁)/[p]_q, …, φ(x_r)/[p]_q}^∧ is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat, hence discrete and [p]_q-torsionfree; with K the minimal complete γ-stable ideal containing J = (I, x₁,…,x_r) one has P/J ≅ E/K, the pair (E, K) is a q-PD pair, and (P, J) → (E, K) is the universal map to a q-PD pair. It depends only on J, commutes with completed base change along maps of q-PD pairs, and its reduction mod q−1 is the classical pd-envelope (Lemma 16.10).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Example 16.9, Lemmas 16.10 and 16.11, pp. 109–111
items.note: Lemma 16.11 characterises the classical pd-envelope ideal as the smallest ideal containing ID and stable under f ↦ f^p/p, which is the q = 1 shadow of the γ-stability condition. Planned by PR.6. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): relative regularity is what Lemma 16.10 assumes.

items.name: The q-crystalline site and its cohomology
items.statement: Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) over (A, (q−1)) and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. The q-crystalline site (R/D)_{q−crys} is the opposite of the category of q-PD pairs (E, J) over (D, I) with a D/I-algebra map R → E/J, with the indiscrete topology; O_{q−crys} sends (E, J) to E and is a presheaf of δ-D-algebras (the paper prints 'δ-B-algebras', sourceIssues E27), and qΩ_{R/D} := RΓ((R/D)_{q−crys}, O_{q−crys}) is a (p,[p]_q)-complete commutative algebra in D(D) with a φ_D-semilinear endomorphism. It is computed by the Čech–Alexander complex of the q-PD envelope of a free δ-D-algebra surjecting onto R (Construction 16.13), and also by smaller Čech–Alexander complexes built from a (p,[p]_q)-completely smooth δ-D-algebra P surjecting onto R, e.g. a (p, I)-completely smooth lift of R along D → D/I (Remark 16.16). Globalisation over a smooth formal scheme is by Zariski descent (Remark 16.15).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Definition 16.12, Construction 16.13 and Remarks 16.15, 16.16, pp. 111–113
items.note: PR.6: 'Construct q-PD pairs, q-crystalline envelopes and the q-crystalline site of BS22 §16. Prove the q-Poincare lemma, framed polynomial computation, change of framing and cocycle descent.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the standing hypotheses of §16.2 were added.

items.name: q-crystalline cohomology specialises to crystalline cohomology
items.statement: Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Then qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) ≅ RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))).
items.note: Theorem 16.18 is the statement that q-crystalline cohomology is prismatic cohomology over the q-de Rham prism. PR.6: 'For p-completely smooth Z_p-algebras, compare the p-completed framed q-de Rham complex with prismatic cohomology after the specified Z_p[zeta_p] base change over (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)). This theorem does not by itself glue all primes into a Habiro theory.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split into 81 (Theorem 16.14), 81b (Theorem 16.17) and 81c (Theorem 16.18).

items.name: Invariance of q-crystalline cohomology under q-PD thickenings
items.statement: Let (D, J) → (D, I) be a morphism of q-PD pairs that is the identity on underlying δ-rings (e.g. J = (q−1)) and R̃ a p-completely smooth D/J-algebra lifting R along D/J → D/I. Then qΩ_{R̃/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 81).

items.name: q-crystalline cohomology is prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Let R be p-completely smooth over D/I and R^{(1)} the p-completely smooth D/([p]_q)-algebra obtained by p-completed base change along the map D/I → D/([p]_q) induced by φ_D. Then ∆_{R^{(1)}/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}, prismatic cohomology being taken relative to the bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 81). The statement that q-crystalline cohomology is prismatic cohomology over the q-de Rham prism.

items.name: q-de Rham complexes compute q-crystalline cohomology
items.statement: Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. A framed D-algebra is a pair (P, S) with P p-completely ind-smooth over D and D[S] → P p-completely ind-étale; the δ-D-algebra structure with δ(X_s) = 0 and the automorphisms γ_s : X_s ↦ qX_s extend uniquely to P, congruent to the identity modulo qX_s − X_s (a nonzerodivisor because D is A-flat), and give q-derivations ∇_{q,s}(f) = (γ_s(f) − f)/(qX_s − X_s) lifting ∂/∂X_s modulo q−1, assembled into the q-de Rham complex qΩ^{*,□}_{P/D} (Construction 16.19). For a framed q-PD datum (P, S, J) these automorphisms extend uniquely to the q-PD envelope (Lemma 16.21) and there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism qΩ_{R/D} ≅ qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} (Theorem 16.22). Combined with Theorem 16.18 this proves the independence, up to canonical quasi-isomorphism, of the q-de Rham complexes of [Sch17] from the choice of coordinates, i.e. [Sch17, Conjecture 1.1]. In Example 1.9 (4): A = ℤ_p⟦q−1⟧, I = ([p]_q), A/I = ℤ_p[ζ_p]; for R p-completely smooth over ℤ_p, R^{(1)} = R ⊗ ℤ_p[ζ_p], X = Spf R^{(1)} and any p-completely étale □ : ℤ_p⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ → R, qΩ^□_R ≅ RΓ_∆(X/A).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Constructions 16.19, 16.20, Lemma 16.21 and Theorem 16.22, Example 1.9 (4), pp. 6 and 114–115
items.note: PR.6 plans exactly this chart computation, and records that 'Habiro HQ.1–2 owns global arithmetic q-de Rham and q-Hodge gluing; it imports these exact local chart computations'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): HQ.1 imports these chart computations from PR.6 ('Import the local q-crystalline site, framed q-difference complex … from PrismaticCohomology PR.6'); it is a consumer. The standing hypotheses and Example 1.9 (4) were added.

items.name: Comparison with the A_inf-cohomology of BMS1
items.statement: Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞} (Example 1.9 (2) is the case C/ℚ_p complete algebraically closed), R a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra, A = A_inf(O_C) (a perfect δ-ℤ_p⟦q−1⟧-algebra, (p, q−1)-completely flat and hence flat), q = [ε] for a compatible system of p-power roots of unity and ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), so that (A, (ξ)) is a q-PD pair. Then there is a canonical isomorphism qΩ_{R/A} ≅ AΩ_R, hence AΩ_R ≅ qΩ_{R/A} ≅ ∆_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ^*_A ∆_{R/A}, as E_∞-A-algebras compatible with Frobenius.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Notation 17.1 and Theorem 17.2, and Example 1.9 (2), pp. 5 and 117
items.note: The Frobenius pullback is essential. Remark 17.3 explains that the proof gives an E₁-comparison which is upgraded to E_∞ by left Kan extension to quasiregular semiperfectoid algebras and quasisyntomic descent. PR.6: 'Construct the explicit all-coordinates comparison with AI.3's AΩ and prove BS22 Theorem 17.2 … The Frobenius pullback is essential.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): §17 assumes only a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}. The comparison map is item 116.

items.name: A criterion for maps compatible with Hodge–Tate data to be isomorphisms
items.statement: Let A be a ring with a nonzerodivisor d, R a smooth A/d-algebra, and E, F derived d-complete commutative algebras in D(A) with E/d, F/d coconnective and H^*(E/d), H^*(F/d) strictly graded commutative, equipped with maps R → H⁰(E/d), R → H⁰(F/d) inducing isomorphisms (Ω^*_{R/(A/d)}, d_dR) ≅ (H^*(E/d), β_d) and likewise for F. Then any commutative A-algebra map E → F intertwining the two is an isomorphism. The same holds if (A, (d)) is a bounded prism, R is p-completely smooth over A/d, and E, F are derived (p, d)-complete; this is the form Theorem 17.2 uses, with d = [p]_q.
items.note: Remarkably, no compatibility with the Frobenius is needed in Theorem 18.2. The consequence is that any diagram of comparison isomorphisms between the theories of this paper necessarily commutes. PR.6: 'Use BS22 §18 to prove independence and compatibility of comparison maps, not merely existence of some quasi-isomorphism.' Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the item was split: Theorem 18.2 is item 84b and Lemma 18.3 item 84c. The 'consequently' linking Lemma 17.4 to Theorem 18.2 is not the paper's: Theorem 18.2 is proved by quasisyntomic descent and Lemma 18.3.

items.name: Prismatic cohomology has no nontrivial endomorphisms
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with perfectoid R = A/I and Sm_R the category of p-completely smooth R-algebras. Let 𝒞_{Sm_R} be the ∞-category of pairs (G, η) with G : Sm_R → 𝒟_{(p,I)-comp}(A) symmetric monoidal and η : id → G ⊗^L_A R a natural transformation of symmetric monoidal functors Sm_R → 𝒟_{p-comp}(R). Prismatic cohomology with its Hodge–Tate map gives ∆_{−/A} ∈ 𝒞_{Sm_R}, and End(∆_{−/A}) = {1}.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Notation 18.1 and Theorem 18.2, p. 122
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 84). No compatibility with Frobenius is needed; any diagram of comparison isomorphisms between the theories of the paper therefore commutes (Leitfaden, pp. 9–10).

items.name: Rigidity of endomorphisms on regular semiperfectoid quotients
items.statement: Let rsPerfd_R be the category of R-algebras that are quotients of p-completely flat perfectoid R-algebras by sequences p-completely regular relative to R. If A-algebra endomorphisms ε_S of ∆_{S/A} (S ∈ rsPerfd_R) are functorial in S and compatible with id_S under η_S : S → ∆̄_{S/A}, then ε_S = id. Theorem 18.2 reduces to this by quasisyntomic Čech descent from Sm_R.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Lemma 18.3 and the proof of Theorem 18.2, pp. 122–123
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 84). The proof uses the Joyal operations δ_n and a saturation argument.

items.name: Koszul complexes and derived completion
items.statement: For a module M with commuting endomorphisms (f_i), the homological Koszul complex Kos(M; (f_i)) represents M ⊗^L_{ℤ[f_i]} ℤ and the cohomological one represents RHom_{ℤ[f_i]}(ℤ, M). For a ring A with a finitely generated ideal I = (f₁,…,f_r), a complex M is derived I-complete if M → R lim_n Kos(M; f₁ⁿ,…,f_rⁿ) is an isomorphism; this is independent of the generators, is checked on cohomology, and gives an abelian category of derived I-complete modules. Classically complete modules are derived complete; conversely a derived complete and I-adically separated module is classically complete; and for principal I and bounded I^∞-torsion the two completions agree.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), §1.2, pp. 10–11, following [Sta, Tag 091N] and [BS15, §§3.4–3.5]
items.note: DD.1 plans 'Derived completion and complete filtered algebra' and is the named owner; AI.1 'owns the derived-completeness interface explicitly'. The Koszul complex is not in the pinned libraries — WORKERS.md lists it among the notions not found — and DD.1 is the layer that plans it for this programme. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): AI.1 was dropped: EnhancedDerivedSheaves E4 says the generic completion construction 'is now canonically DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1'. Mathlib has classical adic completeness and completion (IsAdicComplete, RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Basic.lean:56; AdicCompletion, :171) but not derived completion or the Koszul complex.

items.name: Completely flat, completely étale and completely smooth maps
items.statement: A complex M over A is I-completely flat if M ⊗^L_A N is concentrated in degree 0 for every I-torsion A-module N, and I-completely faithfully flat if moreover M ⊗^L_A A/I is faithfully flat over A/I; M has finite I-complete Tor amplitude if M ⊗^L_A A/I has finite Tor amplitude. A derived I-complete A-algebra R is I-completely étale, smooth or ind-smooth if R ⊗^L_A A/I is so over A/I. D_{I-comp}(−) is a sheaf for I-completely faithfully flat maps of simplicial commutative rings.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), §1.2, pp. 11–12 and its footnotes
items.note: The completed flatness vocabulary in which every hypothesis of the paper is stated. The paper sketches a derived-deformation-theory proof of the Elkik algebraization statement in a footnote. Planned by DD.1 together with PR.0's flatness requirements. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Elkik's algebraization (a completely étale or smooth algebra is the completion of an étale or smooth one) was split off as item 86b: no layer plans it. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): DD.1 plans these notions ('complete flatness and complete faithful-flat descent'). Mathlib has only the uncompleted Algebra.Etale and Algebra.Smooth (RingTheory/Etale/Basic.lean:206, Smooth/Basic.lean:540).

items.name: Elkik's algebraization of completely étale and smooth algebras
items.statement: For a ring A with a finitely generated ideal I, a derived I-complete A-algebra R is I-completely étale (resp. smooth) if and only if it is the derived I-completion of an étale (resp. smooth) A-algebra. The paper's footnote gives a proof by derived deformation theory without noetherian hypotheses.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), §1.2, p. 11 and its footnote; used in Lemma 2.18, p. 17
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 86). No stage mentions Elkik. A source of DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1, using DD.0's deformation theory (route 5).

items.name: Simplicial commutative rings and derived ∞-categories
items.statement: Simplicial commutative rings are used to resolve algebras by ind-smooth ones, to define the cotangent complex, and to form derived pushouts; a simplicial ring is discrete if π_i = 0 for i > 0. For a commutative or E_∞-ring A, D(A) denotes its derived ∞-category and D_{I-comp}(A) the full subcategory of I-complete objects; flatness for M ∈ D(A) means flatness of M ⊗^L_A π₀(A).
items.note: WORKERS.md lists animated (simplicial commutative) rings and stable ∞-categories among the notions not found in the pinned libraries. EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5 is the named owner of simplicial commutative algebra, which Q0 imports, and PR.2 insists on distinguishing 'the animated functor from the classical site cohomology of pi_0'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the owner is the substage E5:animation ('Construct animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings, polynomial resolutions, sifted left Kan extensions and tensor pushouts'); PR.2 consumes it. Simplicial commutative δ-rings, which the paper also uses without definition, are item 97.

items.name: Witt vectors and the Teichmüller expansion
items.statement: The p-typical Witt vectors W(R), their truncations W_n(R), Frobenius, Verschiebung and the Teichmüller map. For R perfect of characteristic p: W(R) is p-torsionfree and p-adically complete, W(R)/p ≅ R, every element is the p-adic sum of its Teichmüller series, and ring maps W(R) → S with p nilpotent in S are determined by their values on Teichmüller representatives.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Remarks 2.4, 2.7, 2.13 and Corollary 2.31, pp. 13–21
items.note: Witt vectors are in the pinned libraries: Mathlib has the p-typical Witt vectors with the ghost components, Frobenius, Verschiebung and Teichmüller map, and WORKERS.md lists them among the notions already present. What is not there is the δ-ring structure on W(R) and the adjunction of Remark 2.7, which are planned at PR.0. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the library claim was narrowed: Mathlib does not have W(R) as the unique p-torsionfree p-complete lift (TeichmullerSeries.lean carries the TODO 'Show that the Teichmuller series is unique'); that universal property is item 9c at PR.0. Citations added and checked: TruncatedWittVector (WittVector/Truncated.lean:62), WittVector.eq_zero_of_p_mul_eq_zero (Complete.lean:55), WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP (:116), WittVector.quotientPEquiv (:105), WittVector.dvd_sub_sum_teichmuller_iterateFrobeniusEquiv_coeff (TeichmullerSeries.lean:93), WittVector.eq_of_apply_teichmuller_eq (:118).

items.name: Perfectoid rings, tilting, A_inf and θ
items.statement: Integral perfectoid rings in the sense of [BMS18, §3], their tilts R^♭, Fontaine's ring A_inf(R) = W(R^♭) and the surjection θ : A_inf(R) → R with its kernel.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 3.10 and §8, pp. 32 and 63
items.note: Q0's integral-algebra prefix plans exactly 'integral perfectoid rings in the scope of BS22, their relation to Tate perfectoid rings and integral subrings, and the necessary A_inf/θ descriptions', keeping ordinary, derived p-adic and pseudouniformizer-adic completions separate; P1 plans perfectoid Tate rings, tilts and untilts. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): partial library coverage: PreTilt (Perfection.lean:634), PreTilt.untilt (Perfectoid/Untilt.lean:49), WittVector.fontaineTheta (Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165) with fontaineTheta_teichmuller (:182) and surjective_fontaineTheta (:195, for R adically complete along p with Frobenius surjective on R/p). There is no integral perfectoid ring and no proof that ker θ is principal; those are planned in Q0:integral-algebra.

items.name: Crystalline cohomology, PD envelopes and the PD Poincaré lemma
items.statement: Divided power structures, PD envelopes, the crystalline site of a scheme relative to a PD base and its cohomology, and the comparison with the de Rham complex of a smooth lift.
items.note: CR.0 plans divided powers and universal thickenings, including PD polynomial algebras and envelopes with their universal properties and the p = 2 subtleties, and CR.1–CR.2 the crystalline site and the PD Poincaré lemma; PR.1 uses CR.2 for the crystalline comparison. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): partial library coverage: DividedPowers (DividedPowers/Basic.lean:78), DPMorphism (DPMorphism.lean:101), DividedPowerAlgebra (DividedPowerAlgebra/Init.lean:100), PadicInt.dividedPowers (DividedPowers/Padic.lean:139). Neither library has PD-envelopes or a crystalline site.

items.name: The cotangent complex and its derived exterior powers
items.statement: The cotangent complex L_{B/A} of a map of simplicial commutative rings, its p-completed variant, the transitivity triangle, and the derived exterior powers ∧^i L with the filtration on the exterior powers of a triangle.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Construction 7.6 and Notation 7.1, pp. 55–57
items.note: DD.0 plans the cotangent complex by simplicial polynomial resolutions with resolution independence, the transitivity triangle, derived base change, and derived symmetric, divided and exterior power functors, and defines quasisyntomic maps by p-complete flatness and mod-p cotangent amplitude. The naive cotangent complex is in Mathlib but the full one is not. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the naive cotangent complex the note mentions is Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex (Extension/Cotangent/Basic.lean:61), with Algebra.H1Cotangent (:552) and KaehlerDifferential (Kaehler/Basic.lean:153).

items.name: The quasisyntomic site and quasisyntomic descent
items.statement: The quasisyntomic site of a p-complete ring, its quasiregular semiperfectoid basis, and descent for p-complete objects along quasisyntomic covers.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Construction 7.6 (3), Theorem 15.3 and §12.4, pp. 57, 92 and 103
items.note: DD.5 plans 'the quasisyntomic site using DD.0's actual morphism condition' and the existence and refinement of the semiperfectoid covers of BMS2 §4, and explicitly assigns the stronger absolutely integrally closed perfectoid extension theorem to PerfectoidQuotients Q3 rather than to itself.

items.name: The décalage functor Lη
items.statement: For a nonzerodivisor f and a termwise f-torsionfree complex K, η_f K is the subcomplex with i-th term the elements of f^iK^i whose differential lies in f^{i+1}K^{i+1}; it descends to Lη_f on the derived category, with its cohomology formula, its lax symmetric monoidal structure and its Bockstein description modulo f.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Theorem 15.3 and Theorem 1.16 (4), pp. 8 and 103, following [BMS18]
items.note: AI.1 is the named owner and PR.3 requires that its 'generic Lη' be used 'independent of the AΩ construction'. AI.1 also warns that Lη is not exact on all triangles and does not commute with all base changes.

items.name: The AΩ-complexes and A_inf-cohomology
items.statement: The complexes AΩ_X of [BMS18], built from the pro-étale sheaf on the generic fibre by applying Lη_µ, with their Frobenius and their crystalline, de Rham and étale specializations.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Example 1.9 (2), Notation 17.1 and Theorem 17.2, pp. 5 and 117
items.note: AI.3 plans 'Integral pro-étale sheaves and the AΩ construction', and AI.7 the Breuil–Kisin descent and cross-theory interfaces; PR.6 states that 'AI.7/CP import the same AΩ comparison and do not reconstruct it'. Remark 1.10 records that the search for the prismatic site was motivated by the desire to explain the origin of the Frobenius on AΩ, which is now simply the Frobenius lift on O_∆. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): AI.7 imports PR.6's comparison ('import PrismaticCohomology PR.6's actual comparison'); it is a consumer, not a planner.

items.name: Topological Hochschild homology, TP and the motivic filtration on K-theory
items.statement: Topological Hochschild homology and its variants TC, TC⁻ and TP with the cyclotomic Frobenius, and the motivic filtration on TC of [BMS19] with graded pieces ℤ_p(n).
items.note: RefinedTraceMethods RT.3 plans the trace and relative comparison and its KU-traces stage the Hochschild and cyclotomic trace constructions; PR.3 records that RT 'proves that BMS2's TC/THH filtration has these graded pieces in its source range' and that it 'does not define Δ by asserting the comparison'. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): the identification of p-adic K-theory with TC [CMM18] was split off as item 95b, which is missing. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): RT.2 plans 'TC, TC⁻ and TP with their comparison maps' and RT.6 the motivic-filtration interface; RT.3 is the Dennis/cyclotomic trace.

items.name: p-adic K-theory is topological cyclic homology for rings henselian along p
items.statement: If S is henselian along pS and S/pS is semiperfect, then K(S; ℤ_p) → τ_{≥0}TC(S; ℤ_p) is an equivalence [CMM18].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 (split from item 95). Owned by the accepted Part II RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs (PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21 route 1, Theorem 4.36 and its consequences; PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 route 1 exports exactly this form). Routed there (route 4).

items.name: Adic spaces and the adic generic fibre of a p-adic formal scheme
items.statement: The adic generic fibre X_η = X ×_{Spf R} Spa(R[1/p], R) of a p-adic formal scheme over a perfectoid ring, as a pre-adic space, its étale site and the nearby-cycles map to X_ét.
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap on adic spaces and AdicEtaleGeometry plan Huber pairs, adic spectra and their étale sites; the paper is careful that X_η is only a pre-adic space in general and that Theorem 11.1 concerns the scheme Spec(R[1/p]), not the adic spectrum. Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22): Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 5 defines adic spaces but not generic fibres. The adic generic-fibre functor is planned in Adic Spaces Part II R2 ('the adic generic-fibre functor', for admissible formal schemes; BS22 needs arbitrary p-adic formal schemes over a perfectoid ring), pre-adic spaces in Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 3 (§3.4), étale sites in AdicEtaleGeometry A1, and nearby cycles in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1.

items.name: Simplicial commutative δ-rings
items.statement: The ∞-category of (derived (p, I)-complete) simplicial commutative δ-rings, with free adjunction of elements (A{x/p}, A{J/I}) and derived pushouts, whose colimits are computed on underlying simplicial commutative rings. The paper uses it without a definition: Corollary 2.39 needs δ-pushouts to be pushouts of simplicial commutative rings in order to apply Lemma 2.38.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Corollary 2.39, p. 25; Corollary 2.44, p. 27; proof of Proposition 3.13, p. 34; Construction 6.1, p. 51
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. No stage mentions simplicial or animated δ-rings. PR.0's 'prismatic envelopes by delta adjunction and derived completion' is the consumer, so it is a source of PR.0 importing EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation.

items.name: Rank-one elements of a δ-ring
items.statement: An element x of a δ-ring has rank one if δ(x) = 0; then φ(x) = x^p, and conversely if the ring is p-torsionfree.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Used in Lemma 2.32, §16 (δ(q) = 0) and §17. the layer's text does not name it, but the layer lists BS22 §§2–3 among its sources and the statement is inside its described scope, so its blueprint must include it.

items.name: A p-complete δ-ring that underlies no prism
items.statement: W(F_p[x]/(x²)) is a p-adically complete δ-ring whose maximal ideal ([x], VW) is killed by [x] ≠ 0, so every nonzerodivisor is a unit and it underlies no prism.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. PR.0's acceptance list asks to 'exhibit a delta-ring that is not a prism'.

items.name: Frobenius-twisted maps to Witt vectors
items.statement: (i) For a derived p-complete δ-ring A with d distinguished, s = can∘w∘φ : A → W(A/d) is a δ-map with s(d) = p·unit (Remark 2.22). (ii) For a prism (A, I), ψ = F∘(A → W(A/I)) carries I into pW(A/I); if W(A/I) is p-torsionfree, ψ is a map of prisms (A, I) → (W(A/I), (p)), J = ker(W(A/I) → A/(I, p)) is a pd-ideal, and ∆_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≅ ∆_{R′/W(A/I)} ≅ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)), whose reduction lifts Ω^*_{R/(A/I)} (proof of Theorem 6.4).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Remark 2.22, p. 18; proof of Theorem 6.4, p. 53
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. The mechanism of the de Rham comparison; PR.1: 'Prove the de Rham comparison after phi_A-twisted reduction'.

items.name: The Cartier isomorphism for polynomial algebras
items.statement: For R = F_p[X₁, …, X_n] there is a natural isomorphism Ω^i_{R^{(1)}/F_p} ≅ H^i(Ω^•_{R/F_p}).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Used in Corollary 5.5, p. 49, and in the proof of Theorem 15.3, p. 104
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Imported. DD.3: 'Compare with classical Cartier on smooth algebras by a coordinate calculation'. Not in the libraries, which have no de Rham complex.

items.name: The de Rham complex of a p-completely smooth formal scheme
items.statement: For X p-completely smooth over A/I, Ω^•_{X/(A/I)} is built from the p-completed Kähler forms; it is the initial strictly graded-commutative differential graded algebra under O_X with d the universal derivation. This universal property is how the Hodge–Tate map η^*_X is built.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Mathlib has Kähler differentials (Kaehler/Basic.lean:153) but no de Rham complex. DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.2 presupposes it ('comparison with the ordinary de Rham complex for smooth maps') without constructing it, so it is a source of DD.2 (route 5).

items.name: Prismatic cohomology of proper smooth formal schemes is perfect
items.statement: For a bounded prism (A, I) and a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I, RΓ_∆(X/A) is a perfect complex of A-modules.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Deduced from the Hodge–Tate comparison and derived Nakayama. PR.1: 'proper smooth perfectness with hypotheses on global sections/finite dimension retained'.

items.name: The A_crys comparison
items.statement: For X smooth over O_C, the [BMS1] comparison of A_inf-cohomology with crystalline cohomology over A_crys follows from Theorem 1.8 (1) and (5) applied to the map of bounded prisms (A_inf, ker θ) → (A_crys, (p)). That map is not the inclusion (ξ ∉ pA_crys): it is can∘φ_{A_inf}, the unique map of prisms (Lemma 4.8) lifting O_C → O_C^♭/p^♭ →^{Frob} O_C^♭/(p^♭)^p → A_crys/p.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. The crystalline comparison and base change of PR.1 give it; AInfCohomology AI.4 builds the A_cris comparison of AΩ, which PR.6 relates to the prismatic one.

items.name: The idempotent-retract lemma
items.statement: Let C be an idempotent complete category, X ∈ C and C_{X/} the category of objects under X. If the identity of C factors over the projection C_{X/} → C through a functor F : C → C_{X/}, then F(X) is an idempotent endomorphism of X and the corresponding retract of X is an initial object of C.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Split off from item 41. PR.2: 'including regular quotient and idempotent-retract arguments in BS22 §§7.7–7.10'.

items.name: Zariski closed subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are strongly Zariski closed
items.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) with R perfectoid Tate, ϖ a topologically nilpotent unit and R⁺ ⊂ R° open and integrally closed. For an ideal I ⊂ R let S be the ϖ-adic completion of R⁺/(I ∩ R⁺), a semiperfectoid ring. Then R′ = S_perfd[1/ϖ] is a perfectoid Tate quotient of R through which every map from R to a perfectoid ring vanishing on I factors uniquely, so V(I) is the strongly Zariski closed Spa(R′, R′⁺), with R′⁺ the smallest open integrally closed subring containing the image of R⁺. This contradicts [Sch15, Rem. II.2.4].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Q4: 'Apply Remark 7.5 to a perfectoid Tate ring R with plus ring R⁺ and an ideal defining a Zariski closed subset'.

items.name: Covers of the final object of (R/A)_∆ by relative perfectoids
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and R → R_∞ a quasisyntomic cover with L_{R_∞/(A/I)} vanishing after derived p-completion (e.g. the perfection of R for a perfect crystalline prism, or R[y_i^{1/p^∞}]^∧/(y_i − x_i) for étale coordinates x_i). Then B = ∆_{R_∞/A} is (p, I)-completely flat and relatively perfect, R_∞ ≅ B/IB, and (B, IB) ∈ (R/A)_∆ covers the final object.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Q3: 'The auxiliary refinements in BS22 7.12–7.15 needed by the chosen proof are included.' Remark 4.5 cites it for F-crystals.

items.name: Covers of the final object of the absolute prismatic site of a regular ring
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism with φ (p, I)-completely flat, and (B, IB) its perfection (Lemma 3.9). Then B/IB is perfectoid and (B, IB) covers the final object of (A/I)_∆; for example, any prism with A/I regular.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. The paper proves it only by 'an argument similar to' Example 7.12. Q3 includes 7.12–7.15.

items.name: Perfectoidization in characteristic p
items.statement: If S is an R-algebra in which p = 0, then S_perfd is the direct-limit perfection S_perf.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Used in the proof of Theorem 9.1. PR.2: 'Construct perfect-prismatic/perfected cohomology'.

items.name: Perfectoidizations are coconnective
items.statement: For any derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S, ∆_{S/A,perf} and S_perfd lie in D^{≥0}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. The proof imports Lurie's P⁰ operation (Rational and p-adic homotopy theory, Rem. 2.2.7). Used in Proposition 8.5 and Corollary 8.14. A source of PR.2 (route 1).

items.name: Tor-independence of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For maps S ← R → T of perfectoid rings, S ⊗̂^L_R T is concentrated in degree 0 and perfectoid, and the corresponding completed tensor product of perfect prisms is a perfect prism.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proof of Lemma 10.3, p. 78; used implicitly in Proposition 8.10
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Deduced from Tor-independence of perfect F_p-algebras, PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/S320 ([BS17, Lemma 3.16]), which an accepted route gives to EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1, by the perfect-prism/perfectoid equivalence of PR.0. A source of PR.0 (route 1).

items.name: Inputs from Bhatt–Mathew: the arc_p-topology and arc-descent
items.statement: (i) The arc_p-topology on p-complete rings [BM18, Def. 6.14] and arc_p-equivalences [BM18, Def. 6.19]; (ii) arc_p-descent for S ↦ RΓ(Spec S[1/p], ℤ/pⁿ) [BM18, Cor. 6.17]; (iii) for any arc-cover Spec B → Spec A of perfect schemes, the Čech complex 0 → A → B → B ⊗_A B → ⋯ is exact ([BS17, Thm 4.1], [BM18, Thm 1.6, Thm 5.16], [BS17, Lemma 6.3]).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proof of Proposition 8.10, p. 68; proof of Theorem 9.1, pp. 71–72
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. These are PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21/130, /133, /135 and /16 in the accepted route 1 of that paper (the new roadmap ArcTopologyAndDescent). Recorded here so that the prismatic consumers name them; route 2 joins that roadmap.

items.name: Étale cohomology of Spec S[1/p] and of Spa(S[1/p], S)
items.statement: For S p-complete, the étale cohomology of Spec S[1/p] agrees with that of the adic spectrum Spa(S[1/p], S) with torsion coefficients [Hub96, Cor. 3.2.2]; for S perfectoid, the étale site of Spa(S[1/p], S) is equivalent to that of its tilt [Sch12, Thm 1.11].
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proof of Theorem 9.1, p. 73
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Tilting of étale sites is planned in PerfectoidSpaces P3 ('Glue the affine tilting equivalence to the equivalence of étale sites, ECD 6.3'). Huber's comparison is in the brief of the accepted route 3 of PAPER-GUO-REINECKE-24 for ArcTopologyAndDescent, so it goes with route 2.

items.name: The Nygaard and conjugate filtrations for p-completely regular semiperfectoid quotients
items.statement: Theorem 12.2 holds for S = R⟨X₁^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f₁, …, f_m) with f₁, …, f_m a p-completely regular sequence.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. Proved with 'good' filtrations (φ(Fil^i_M) ⊂ d^i∆_S, with φ/d^i identifying gr^i_M with Fil_i ∆̄_S), their uniqueness, base change and faithfully flat descent along relatively perfect maps, the Künneth formula from S(1), and André's lemma. Used in §13 and in Theorem 15.2. PR.3: 'On the discrete quasiregular semiperfectoid calculation construct Nygaard pieces by the actual Frobenius-divisibility condition'.

items.name: The syntomic complexes ℤ_p(n)
items.statement: For n ≥ 0 and S p-complete quasisyntomic, ℤ_p(n)(S) := fib(N^{≥n}∆̂_S{n} →^{1−φ_n} ∆̂_S{n}), with ∆̂_S the Nygaard-completed prismatic cohomology of [BMS19] (through THH and quasisyntomic descent; over a perfectoid base the Nygaard completion of ∆_S, by Theorem 13.1). For S quasiregular semiperfectoid over O_C, ℤ_p(n)(S) ≃ fib(Fil^n_N∆_S →^{1−φ_n} ∆_S).
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), §14, p. 97, and the proof of Theorem 14.1, p. 100
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. PR.4: 'Construct the syntomic/Tate-twist fibers from Nygaard pieces and divided Frobenius with the intrinsic twists'; RT.6 owns the motivic-filtration side.

items.name: The comparison map from q-crystalline cohomology to AΩ
items.statement: For R very small (R/p generated over O_C/p by units), S = R^* and 𝒞_S the filtered poset of finite Σ ⊂ S generating R: take P_Σ = A[x_s^{±1}]^∧ with δ(x_s) = 0 and γ_s(x_s) = qx_s. Then qΩ_{R/A} ≃ colim_Σ Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); ∇_{q,s}) and AΩ_R ≃ colim_Σ η_{q−1}Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); σ_s − 1). The universal property of q-PD envelopes gives a δ-A-map μ₀ : D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) intertwining γ_s and σ_s, from which μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R comes by Kos_c(∇_q) ≅ η_{q−1}Kos_c(γ_s − 1); it is glued over very small opens.
items.locator: arXiv:1905.08229v4 (12 January 2022), Proof of Theorem 17.2, pp. 117–120
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. PR.6: 'Construct the explicit all-coordinates comparison with AI.3's AΩ and prove BS22 Theorem 17.2'. The proof also uses [Bha18b, Lemma 5.14] and [Bha20, Lemma 5.15].

items.name: The cotangent complex as the first Nygaard graded piece
items.statement: For any formal A/I-scheme X, L_{X/A} ≃ gr¹_N ∆^{(1)}_{X/A}[1] (by left Kan extension of Proposition 4.15 and Theorem 1.16 (3); the paper prints the identification without the shift and cites Theorem 1.16 (2); sourceIssues E26).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22. PR.3: 'Prove the associated-graded description'. It upgrades Proposition 4.15 (item 29).

prerequisites.citation: Bhargav Bhatt and Akhil Mathew, The arc-topology, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1899–1988
prerequisites.why: The arc-topology of §8 (Definition 8.7, Proposition 8.10) and the arc_p-topology and arc_p-descent [BM18, Def. 6.14, Cor. 6.17, Def. 6.19] used in the proof of Theorem 9.1. Now covered: PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21 is extracted and reviewed (accept), and its route 1 proposes the new roadmap ArcTopologyAndDescent, to which route 2 here belongs.

prerequisites.citation: Akhil Mathew, The Galois group of a stable homotopy theory, Adv. Math. 291 (2016), 403–541
prerequisites.why: The notion of descendability used in Lemma 8.6, with [BS17, §11.2, Lemma 11.22] for the index bound. Now covered: the accepted route 6 of PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17 gives descendability to EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract.

prerequisites.citation: Dustin Clausen, Akhil Mathew and Matthew Morrow, K-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 34 (2021), no. 2, 411–473
prerequisites.why: The identification of p-adic K-theory with topological cyclic homology which converts Theorem 14.1 into the evenness of K-theory (Corollary 14.2; also the footnote in Remark 9.5). Now covered: PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21 is accepted, and its route 1 is the Part II to which route 4 here belongs.

prerequisites.citation: Yves André, La conjecture du facteur direct, Publ. Math. IHÉS 127 (2018), 71–93
prerequisites.why: The flatness lemma reproved prismatically as Theorem 7.14. Covered by PAPER-ANDRE-18-B (accepted).

prerequisites.citation: Yves André, Le lemme d'Abhyankar perfectoïde, Publ. Math. IHÉS 127 (2018), 1–70
prerequisites.why: The perfectoid Abhyankar lemma that Theorem 10.9 improves on, and Proposition 1.9.1, quoted as Proposition 10.8 without its flatness assumption on m ⊗ m. PAPER-ANDRE-18 is under revision (its route 1 is accepted).

prerequisites.citation: Ofer Gabber and Lorenzo Ramero, Almost Ring Theory, Lecture Notes in Math. 1800, Springer, 2003
prerequisites.why: The basic setup of almost mathematics, the flatness hypothesis of §2.5.15 which the ideal J_perfd is checked to satisfy, and the almost finiteness notions used in Proposition 10.8. PerfectoidSpaces P0 plans almost ring theory but the book itself is not covered. The paper also cites Gabber–Ramero, Foundations for almost ring theory, Theorem 16.9.17 (p. 62). PerfectoidSpaces P5 already cites Almost Ring Theory 5.4.53.

prerequisites.citation: Raymond Heitmann and Linquan Ma, Extended plus closure in complete local rings, J. Algebra 571 (2021), 134–150 (arXiv:1708.05761)
prerequisites.why: Remark 10.13 reproves [HM17, Theorem 1.3] ('the main theorems of [HM17] follow almost immediately') from Theorem 10.9. The extraction had cited Hochster–Ma and a different Heitmann–Ma paper (arXiv:1703.08281), which BS22 does not cite.

prerequisites.citation: Jacob Lurie, Spectral Algebraic Geometry, preprint
prerequisites.why: The ∞-categorical foundations used in §1.2: derived completion (SAG §§7–8), flat descent for simplicial commutative rings (Corollary D.6.3.3) and the identification D_{I-comp}(B) ≃ lim_n D(Kos(B; f^n)) (Theorem 8.3.4.4, Remark 8.3.4.5). Appendix D of SAG supplies the descent statements.

prerequisites.citation: André Joyal, δ-anneaux et vecteurs de Witt, C. R. Math. Rep. Acad. Sci. Canada 7 (1985), 177–182; James Borger, Witt vectors, lambda-rings, and arithmetic jet spaces (lecture notes), and The basic geometry of Witt vectors I, Algebra Number Theory 5 (2011), 231–285
prerequisites.why: The origin of δ-rings, the identification of the right adjoint to the forgetful functor with the Witt vector functor, and the δ_n operations of Remark 2.13; Borger's work identifies δ-structures with p-typical λ-structures. PR.0 plans δ-rings but the sources are not covered.

prerequisites.citation: Charles Rezk, Étale extensions of λ-rings, preprint (2014)
prerequisites.why: The description of a δ-structure as a section of W₂(R) → R used in Remark 2.4 and, through the pullback square of Remark 2.5, the identification of δ-structures with derived Frobenius lifts.

prerequisites.citation: Renée Elkik, Solutions d'équations à coefficients dans un anneau hensélien, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4) 6 (1973), 553–603
prerequisites.why: The algebraization results that identify I-completely étale and I-completely smooth algebras with derived completions of étale and smooth algebras; the paper sketches an alternative derived-deformation-theory proof in a footnote to §1.2 because Elkik assumes noetherian hypotheses. It is not in the paper's bibliography: the paper names 'Elkik's algebraization' without a reference, in §1.2 and in the proof of Lemma 2.18 (p. 17).

prerequisites.citation: Peter Scholze, Canonical q-deformations in arithmetic geometry, Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse Math. (6) 26 (2017), no. 5, 1163–1192
prerequisites.why: The q-de Rham complexes and Conjecture 1.1 on their independence of coordinates, which Theorems 16.18 and 16.22 resolve; it is the motivation for the whole of §16.

prerequisites.citation: Bhargav Bhatt and Jacob Lurie, Absolute prismatic cohomology (cited as 'in preparation')
prerequisites.why: Cited only in footnote 9 to Remark 4.13 (prismatic crystals) and in Remark 9.5, for the purely algebraic prismatic logarithm that replaces the cyclotomic-trace construction of the comparison map of Theorem 9.4. PR.5 plans the absolute theory and names Bhatt–Lurie as its source. The Prismatization paper (arXiv:2201.06124), which the extraction had added, is not cited.

prerequisites.citation: Pierre Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline des schémas de caractéristique p > 0, Lecture Notes in Math. 407, Springer (1974)
prerequisites.why: §III.4 (Proposition III.4.1.4) is used in the proof of Theorem 5.2. CrystallineCohomology CR.0–CR.1 name Berthelot as a source.

prerequisites.citation: Jean-Marc Fontaine and William Messing, p-adic periods and p-adic étale cohomology, Contemp. Math. 67 (1987), 179–207
prerequisites.why: Cited on p. 6 as motivation for Theorems 1.12 and 1.14 (the syntomic approach of §§7 and 12). The extraction's entry named Timmerscheidt and Berthelot–Ogus, whom the paper does not cite, and a DOI that does not resolve.

The paper is the named source of PR.0 (BS22 §§2–3), PR.2 (§§7–8) and PR.4 (§§9, 11, 14); these items are the results those layers must add beyond what their texts plan. routes.title: The arc-topology and descent for étale cohomology
routes.brief: This route adds a source to the new roadmap proposed by the accepted PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21 route 1 (ArcTopologyAndDescent, 'The arc-topology and descent for étale cohomology'), which owns the arc-topology and arc-descent; it is reused, not proposed again. Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology (arXiv:1905.08229v4) §8.2 and §9 add the p-adic variant and its perfectoid basis, which that design must export in the following forms. Definition 8.7: on p-adic formal schemes, Y → X (qcqs) is an arc-cover if for every p-adically complete rank-one valuation ring V with Spf V → X there are a faithfully flat extension V ⊂ W of such rings and a lift Spf W → Y; open covers and arc-covers generate the topology. Lemma 8.8 and Remark 8.9: every p-adic formal scheme has an arc-cover by a perfectoid one, indeed by a product of p-complete rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field. Proposition 8.10: on perfectoids, O is an arc-sheaf with H^i_arc(Spf R, O) = 0 for i > 0, and X ↦ Hom(X, T) is an arc-sheaf for every p-adic formal scheme T. The inputs are Bhatt–Mathew's arc_p-topology, arc_p-descent for S ↦ RΓ(Spec S[1/p], ℤ/pⁿ) and arc-descent for perfect schemes (item 112, which are that paper's items /130, /133, /135 and /16), and Huber's comparison of the étale cohomology of Spec S[1/p] and Spa(S[1/p], S) (item 113, already in the accepted PAPER-GUO-REINECKE-24 route 3 brief). routes.title: Perfectoid quotients and their prismatic prerequisites, Part II: perfectoidization of integral algebras and almost purity along arbitrary ideals
routes.brief:
Start after Perfectoid quotients and their prismatic prerequisites (PerfectoidQuotients) Q2–Q4, which construct the universal perfectoidization of semiperfectoid rings, André's flatness lemma (Theorem 7.14) and the surjectivity of S → S_perfd (Theorem 7.4). This Part II develops the perfectoidization of arbitrary p-complete rings over a perfectoid ring and the almost purity theorem along an arbitrary ideal, from Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology (arXiv:1905.08229v4) §§8.1–8.2 and §10.

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 10.11: let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, I) and R → S the p-completion of an integral map; then ∆_{S/A,perf} is discrete and a perfect p-complete δ-A-algebra, so S_perfd is discrete and perfectoid and S → S_perfd is the universal map to a perfectoid ring. Theorem 10.9: let J ⊂ R be finitely generated and S a finitely presented finite R-algebra with Spec S → Spec R finite étale outside V(J); then S_perfd is discrete and perfectoid, S → S_perfd is an isomorphism away from V(J), and R/pⁿ → S_perfd/pⁿ is almost finite projective and almost unramified for the almost setting (R/pⁿ, J_{perfd,n}); if S has a G-action that is G-Galois outside V(J), R → S_perfd is a J-almost G-Galois cover. Corollary 8.11: S_perfd = RΓ_arc(Spf S, O). Corollary 8.12: the excision pullback square (S_perfd, S′_perfd, (S/I)_perfd, (S′/I)_perfd) when S → S′ is an isomorphism of arc-sheaves outside I. Proposition 8.5: the perfect prismatic site computes ∆_{S/A,perf}, so S_perfd = lim_{S → R′} R′ over maps to perfectoid rings.

Construct here: Proposition 8.5 (it needs Theorems 7.4 and 7.14, which is why it cannot sit in PR.2); Corollaries 8.11 and 8.12; J-almost mathematics for a derived p-complete ideal J of a perfectoid ring (J_perfd, Propositions 10.2 and 10.4, Lemma 10.3), the connectivity criterion (Lemma 10.5), J-almost Galois extensions (Definition 10.6, Remark 10.7), Theorem 10.9 in its almost and exact forms, the stratification Lemma 10.12, Theorem 10.11, and Remark 10.13 (Heitmann–Ma, Extended plus closure, Theorem 1.3). Import, never re-plan: PrismaticCohomology PR.2 (Definition 8.2, Lemmas 8.4 and 8.6, Proposition 8.13, Corollary 8.14); PerfectoidQuotients Q2, Q3 and Q4; ArcTopologyAndDescent (Definition 8.7 and Proposition 8.10, route 2); PerfectoidSpaces P0 for the abstract almost setup and Proposition 10.8 (route 6); PrismaticCohomology PR.0 for Tor-independence of perfectoid rings. Export to PrismaticCohomology PR.4 (Theorem 9.1 needs Corollary 8.11, Theorem 11.1 needs Theorem 10.11) and PerfectoidSpaces P8. Remark 10.10 is the point to keep: the proof avoids adic and perfectoid spaces, so for J = (p) it is a new proof of the classical almost purity theorem, and for J = (g) it improves André's perfectoid Abhyankar lemma. Do not identify J-almost mathematics with the pseudouniformizer almost mathematics of PerfectoidSpaces P1–P2 except for J = (p).

routes.title: Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods, Part II: K-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs
routes.brief: This route adds a source to the Part II of Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods proposed by the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction (RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs), which owns the rigidity of K^inv for henselian pairs (their Theorem A). Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology (arXiv:1905.08229v4) uses it in the form exported for PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19: if S is henselian along pS and S/pS is semiperfect, then K(S; ℤ_p) → τ_{≥0}TC(S; ℤ_p) is an equivalence (item 95b). With the motivic filtration of RefinedTraceMethods RT.6 and Theorem 14.1 (ℤ_p(n) discrete and p-torsionfree, planned in PrismaticCohomology PR.4), it gives Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 (item 70b): locally on the quasisyntomic site of any quasisyntomic ℤ_p-algebra, K(−; ℤ_p) and K(−)/p are concentrated in even degrees, and π_*K(O_C/pⁿ; ℤ_p) vanishes in odd degrees. Import PR.4 and RT.6; neither depends on this Part II.
